Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- codemyspec:design: Architecture design, UI design system, and technology strategy. Use before writing code to plan how to build it.
- codemyspec:develop: Full-lifecycle development — context orchestration, LiveView orchestration, and interactive refactoring. Spawns subagents for multi-step workflows.
- codemyspec:implement: Autonomous implementation loop — start or stop requirements-driven development. The agent walks the requirement graph automatically.
- codemyspec:init: Project setup, authentication, and sync. Use when starting a new project, logging in, or refreshing stale state.
- codemyspec:next: Find and start the next requirement task in one gesture. Use after each completed task as your single onboarding instruction.
- codemyspec:product: Product management — guided story interview, review, and Three Amigos sessions. Use when defining what to build, refining requirements, reviewing story quality, or running an Example Mapping session on a story.
- codemyspec:qa: QA testing and issue management — full app QA, per-story QA, integration planning, issue triage, and fixes.
- codemyspec:sync: Sync project components and regenerate architecture views. Use after git pulls, before design sessions, or when views feel stale.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # No `:protect_from_forgery` — unlike the GET-only public routes below
  # (which can just use `:browser`), `/pay/:token` accepts a POST from a
  # client with no session and no CSRF token (a mailed or shared link).
  # `:fetch_current_scope_for_user` still runs — the root layout reads
  # `@current_scope` unconditionally, and this plug assigns `nil` when
  # no one's logged in rather than requiring an authenticated visitor.
  pipeline :public do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :webhook do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # Office-only controller routes (e.g. the payroll CSV export) layer
  # this on top of `:require_authenticated_user`; office-only
  # LiveViews use the equivalent `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole`
  # on_mount hook instead, since a plug can't gate a live_session.
  pipeline :require_office_role do
    plug CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authentication routes

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
      live "/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit
      live "/users/settings/confirm-email/:token", UserLive.Settings, :confirm_email

      live "/accounts", AccountLive.Index, :index
      live "/accounts/new", AccountLive.Form, :new
      live "/accounts/:id/edit", AccountLive.Form, :edit
      live "/accounts/picker", AccountLive.Picker, :index
      live "/accounts/:id", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/manage", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/members", AccountLive.Members, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/invitations", AccountLive.Invitations, :show

      live "/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index

      live "/field", FieldLive.Today, :index
      live "/field/jobs/:id", FieldLive.Job, :show
    end

    # Office-only surfaces: dispatch, payroll, quality, invoicing,
    # clients, quotes, reminders, and the audit trail. Gated to
    # owners/admins by `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole` — a cleaner
    # is redirected to `/field` instead. See that module for why it's
    # a separate `live_session` from the one above.
    live_session :require_office_role,
      on_mount: [
        {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole, :default}
      ] do
      live "/clients", ClientLive.Index, :index
      live "/clients/new", ClientLive.Index, :new
      live "/clients/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit
      live "/clients/:id/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_client_property
      live "/clients/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show
      live "/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_property
      live "/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property
      live "/properties/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show_property

      live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
      live "/schedule/plans/new", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :new
      live "/schedule/plans/:id/edit", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :edit
      live "/schedule/jobs/new", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :new
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id/assign", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :assign
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/new", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :new
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:id", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:cleaner_id/time-off/new", ScheduleLive.AvailabilityLive, :new

      live "/audit", AuditLive, :index

      live "/quotes", QuoteLive.Index, :index
      live "/quotes/new", QuoteLive.Builder, :new
      live "/quotes/:id", QuoteLive.Builder, :show

      live "/quality", QualityLive.Review, :index
      live "/quality/scorecards", QualityLive.Scorecards, :index
      live "/quality/templates", QualityLive.Templates, :index
      live "/quality/templates/new", QualityLive.Templates, :new
      live "/quality/templates/:id/edit", QualityLive.Templates, :edit
      live "/quality/:job_id", QualityLive.Review, :show

      live "/timesheets", TimesheetLive, :index

      live "/invoices", InvoiceLive.Index, :index
      live "/invoices/:id", InvoiceLive.Show, :show

      live "/reminders", ReminderLive, :index
    end

    post "/users/update-password", UserSessionController, :update_password
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user, :require_office_role]

    get "/timesheets/export", TimesheetExportController, :show
  end

  scope "/integrations/oauth", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    get "/:provider", IntegrationsController, :request
    get "/callback/:provider", IntegrationsController, :callback
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :current_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/users/register", UserLive.Registration, :new
      live "/users/log-in", UserLive.Login, :new
      live "/users/log-in/:token", UserLive.Confirmation, :new
      live "/invitations/accept/:token", InvitationsLive.Accept, :new
    end

    post "/users/log-in", UserSessionController, :create
    delete "/users/log-out", UserSessionController, :delete

    # Public confirm/reschedule links a client reaches from their
    # reminder — no login, so `:browser` (not `:require_authenticated_user`)
    # like the routes above. Plain `:browser`, not `:public`, so
    # `fetch_current_scope_for_user` still assigns `current_scope` for
    # the root layout.
    get "/reminders/confirm/:token", ReminderController, :confirm
    get "/reminders/reschedule/:token", ReminderController, :reschedule
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :public

    get "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :show
    post "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :create
  end

  scope "/webhooks", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :webhook

    post "/stripe", StripeWebhookController, :create
    post "/twilio", TwilioWebhookController, :status
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story848.Criterion7215Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 848 — Get an instant quote from the public website
  Criterion 7215 — Building a quote with room counts shows a price
  with no contact info: a real price is shown from selecting a
  service type and room counts alone, before any name, email, or
  phone is entered.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "the public quote form prices a per-room home before contact info is given" do
    scenario "building a quote with room counts shows a price with no contact info" do
      given_ "a business with a per-room rate card and a visitor on the public quote page",
             context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})

        Fixtures.rate_card_fixture(scope, %{
          per_room_bedroom_rate_cents: 5000,
          per_room_bathroom_rate_cents: 3000
        })

        {:ok, quote_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/book")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :quote_live, quote_live)}
      end

      when_ "the visitor selects a service type, bedroom count, and bathroom count without entering a name, email, or phone",
            context do
        html =
          context.quote_live
          |> form("[data-test='quote-form']",
            quote: %{pricing_model: "per_room", bedroom_count: 3, bathroom_count: 2}

          |> render_change()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :html, html)}

      then_ "a real price computed from the rate card is displayed immediately", context do
        assert has_element?(context.quote_live, "[data-test='quote-total']", "$210.00")
        refute has_element?(context.quote_live, "[data-test='unsupported-quote-message']")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

        |> Plug.Conn.put_req_header("content-type", "application/json")
        |> post("/webhooks/stripe", payload)
        |> Phoenix.ConnTest.json_response(200)

        owner_conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn(), user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{lead: lead, account: account, owner_conn: owner_conn})}
      end

      when_ "the confirmation completes", context do
        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the visit appears as scheduled for both the business and the client, and the client receives a confirmation containing a magic-link to their portal",
            context do
        {:ok, accept_live, _html} =
          live(context.conn, ~p"/book/accept/#{context.lead.acceptance_token}")

        assert has_element?(accept_live, "[data-test='booking-confirmed']")

        {:ok, board_live, _html} = live(context.owner_conn, ~p"/schedule")
        assert render(board_live) =~ context.lead.client_name

        assert_email_sent(fn email ->
          email.to == [{"", context.lead.client_email}] and
            email.html_body =~ ~r{href="[^"]*portal[^"]*"}i
        end)

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

  # completion every time — a sanctioned shortcut per
  # bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def client_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, client} =
      CleanerCrm.Clients.create_client(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          name: "Client #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}",
          card_on_file: false,
          email: "client#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com",
          phone: "+15555550100"
        })
      )

    client
  end

  def job_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    attrs = Enum.into(attrs, %{})
    start_time = Map.get(attrs, :start_time, ~T[09:00:00])

    {:ok, job} =
      CleanerCrm.Scheduling.create_job(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          agreed_price: Decimal.new("150.00"),
          status: :scheduled,
          scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 7),
          start_time: start_time,
          # Some specs override `start_time` alone (e.g. pinning it to a
          # lead-time boundary) without overriding `end_time` — a fixed
          # `~T[11:00:00]` default would then land before an overridden
          # start_time and fail the "end after start" changeset check.
          end_time: default_end_time(start_time)
        })
      )

    # Notifications (story 837) — the automatic reminder trigger is a
    # periodic Oban-cron scan in production (see the background-jobs
    # ADR); nothing about creating a job through this fixture would
    # otherwise run that scan within a spec's lifetime. Running it here
    # is a no-op for every job outside its owning account's configured
    # lead-time window (and a no-op entirely for accounts that never
    # configured reminders), so it's safe for every other story's jobs
    # while making story 837's own boundary-timed fixtures deterministic.
    CleanerCrm.Notifications.send_due_reminders()

    job
  end

  # `given_` blocks bind `scope` from `user_scope_fixture/1` *before*
  # `account_fixture/2` creates the account, so it never carries an
  # `active_account_id` — every fixture below that scopes a context
  # call by account needs to resolve it from the user's membership at
  # call time instead of trusting the scope it was handed.
  defp scoped_to_account(%CleanerCrm.Users.Scope{active_account_id: nil, user: user} = scope) do
    case CleanerCrm.Accounts.MembersRepository.list_user_accounts(user.id) do
      [account | _] -> %{scope | active_account_id: account.id, active_account: account}
      [] -> scope
    end
  end

  defp scoped_to_account(scope), do: scope

  # Two hours after `start_time`, unless that would wrap past midnight
  # (into an earlier clock time), in which case the day just ends there.
  defp default_end_time(start_time) do
    candidate = Time.add(start_time, 2 * 3600, :second)
    if Time.compare(candidate, start_time) == :gt, do: candidate, else: ~T[23:59:59]
  end

  def job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope = scoped_to_account(scope)
    job = job_fixture(scope, client, Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :completed}))

    {:ok, _checklist} =
      CleanerCrm.Quality.complete_checklist(scope, job, [
        %{
          task: "Kitchen counters wiped down",
          before_photo: "before_kitchen.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_kitchen.jpg"
        },
        %{
          task: "Bathrooms sanitized",
          before_photo: "before_bath.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_bath.jpg"
        }
      ])

    job
  end

  def invoice_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, invoice} =
      CleanerCrm.Billing.create_invoice(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          amount: job.agreed_price,
          status: :unpaid
        })
      )

    invoice
  end

  # Time tracking (story 838) — a resolved clock-in/out record for a
  # job.
  #
  # Clocking in and out through the UI is covered end-to-end by story
  # 838's own "cleaner clocks in and out of an assigned job" spec
  # (drives FieldLive.Job). Scenarios whose subject is a downstream pay
  # calculation (hourly vs. piece-rate, running pay-period totals,
  # payroll CSV export) seed the resolved time entry directly here
  # instead of re-driving the clock-in/out flow every time — a
  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def time_entry_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, time_entry} =
      CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.create_time_entry(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-08 09:00:00Z],
          clocked_out_at: ~U[2024-01-08 12:00:00Z]
        })
      )

    time_entry
  end

  # Notifications (story 837) — an already-sent appointment reminder
  # with its confirm/reschedule token.
  #
  # The automatic "reminder sent at the configured lead time" trigger
  # is covered end-to-end by story 837's own "reminder fires at the
  # configured lead time" spec. Scenarios whose subject is a
  # downstream decision on an existing reminder (confirm, reschedule,
  # delivery-status fallback) seed the already-sent notification
  # directly here instead of re-driving the scheduler trigger every
  # time — a sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def notification_fixture(scope, client, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, notification} =
      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          job_id: job.id,
          kind: :reminder,
          channel: :email,
          status: :sent,
          token: "reminder_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
        })
      )

    notification
  end

  # Schedule alerts (story 843) — a pending schedule-change
  # notification already pushed to a cleaner.
  #
  # The push itself (a moved or cancelled job creating this
  # notification) is covered end-to-end by story 843's own "moved job
  # notifies the cleaner" / "cancelled job notifies the cleaner"
  # specs, which drive the real trigger via `ScheduleLive.Board`.
  # Scenarios whose subject is a downstream decision on an existing
  # pending change (acknowledging, re-prompting, office visibility,
  # escalation, channel fallback) seed the already-pushed notification
  # directly here instead of re-driving the board move every time — a
  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md. Never pass
  # `status: :acknowledged` here — the acknowledgment round-trip
  # through `FieldLive.Today` is the whole point of story 843.
  def schedule_change_notification_fixture(scope, cleaner, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, notification} =
      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
          job_id: job.id,
          kind: :schedule_change,
          channel: :push,
          status: :pending,
          change_summary: "Job schedule changed",
          pushed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
          token: "schedule_change_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
        })
      )

    notification
  end

  # Quality (story 839) — a job carrying an unfinished, per-job
  # checklist of required and optional tasks.
  #
  # Checking items off and completing the job through the checklist UI
  # is the subject under test in `FieldLive.Job`, so this fixture stops
  # short of that — it only seeds the checklist itself. Sanctioned
  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md: `ChecklistTemplate` assignment
  # (story 842) has its own creation flow this fixture skips.
  def job_with_checklist_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope = scoped_to_account(scope)

    job =
      job_fixture(
        scope,
        client,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :in_progress, cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
      )

    {:ok, checklist} =
      CleanerCrm.Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, [
        %{task: "Kitchen counters wiped down", required: true},
        %{task: "Bathrooms sanitized", required: true},
        %{task: "Fridge interior wiped down", required: false}
      ])

    %{job: job, checklist: checklist}
  end

  # Quality (story 842) — a job carrying an unfinished, room-grouped
  # checklist whose items are exactly what the caller passes in.
  #
  # Story 842 owns the `ChecklistTemplate` -> per-job `Checklist`
  # assignment flow (which room/task combinations count as in scope for
  # a given job). That assignment UI doesn't exist yet and isn't part
  # of this story's component list (only `FieldLive.ChecklistComponent`
  # is), so seeding the already-instantiated, room-tagged checklist
  # directly is the sanctioned bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — the
  # subject under test is opening/working the checklist on
  # `FieldLive.Job`, not how it got assigned. `items` is a list of
  # `%{room:, task:, required:}` maps; a spec proving an out-of-scope
  # task never appears simply omits it from `items`.
  def job_with_room_checklist_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, items, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope = scoped_to_account(scope)

    job =
      job_fixture(
        scope,
        client,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :in_progress, cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
      )

    {:ok, checklist} = CleanerCrm.Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, items)

    %{job: job, checklist: checklist}
  end

  # Client portal (stories 851, 852) — an already-established client
  # portal session.
  #
  # The magic-link exchange itself (`/portal/access/:token`) is covered
  # end-to-end by story 850's own specs. Downstream portal stories
  # whose subject is what a client can do once inside the portal seed
  # the session directly here instead of re-driving that exchange
  # every time — a sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  # Assumes `CleanerCrmWeb.PortalAuth` reads the client id from the
  # `:portal_client_id` session key (mirroring `:user_token` for staff
  # auth).
  def portal_session_fixture(client) do
    Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn()
    |> Phoenix.ConnTest.init_test_session(%{})
    |> Plug.Conn.put_session(:portal_client_id, client.id)
  end

  # Reschedule/cancel policy (story 851) — the account's configured
  # notice window and fees.
  #
  # The client-facing decision (on-time, late, or same-day) is the
  # subject under test, so this only seeds the account's stated
  # policy, never a per-job fee outcome.
  def cancellation_policy_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, policy} =
      CleanerCrm.Scheduling.set_cancellation_policy(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          notice_window_hours: 48,
          late_fee_cents: 2_500,
          same_day_fee_cents: 5_000
        })
      )

    policy
  end

  # Quoting (story 848) — the account's public-facing rate card, set
  # directly rather than through the office `QuoteLive.Builder` rate
  # card form (covered end-to-end by story 835) since these specs'
  # subject is the public instant-quote calculator reading it, not the
  # office save flow. Extra keys the current `RateCard` schema doesn't
  # persist yet (frequency discounts, add-on pricing) are accepted
  # here so specs can drive the pricing config story 848 needs once
  # the schema grows to hold it.
  def rate_card_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope = scoped_to_account(scope)
    rate_card = CleanerCrm.Quoting.get_or_create_rate_card(scope)
    {:ok, rate_card} = CleanerCrm.Quoting.update_rate_card(scope, rate_card, attrs)
    rate_card
  end

  # Booking (story 849) — an instant quote already accepted by the
  # client (contact captured, price locked). The quote-to-accepted
  # transition itself is covered end-to-end by story 848's own
  # "instant quote price matches the later acceptance total" spec, so
  # scenarios whose subject is the slot/policy/card steps that follow
  # seed the accepted lead directly here instead of re-driving the
  # quote calculator every time — a sanctioned shortcut per
  # bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def lead_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, lead} =
      CleanerCrm.Booking.create_lead(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          pricing_model: :per_room,
          bedroom_count: 3,
          bathroom_count: 2,
          frequency: :one_time,
          total_cents: 19_500,
          status: :accepted,
          client_name: "Dana Prescott",
          client_email: "dana-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com",
          client_phone: "+15555550100"
        })
      )

    lead
  end

  # Portal (story 850) — an already-issued, not-yet-exchanged
  # magic-link token for a client, distinct from `portal_session_fixture/1`
  # above (which bypasses straight to an established session for
  # downstream stories 851/852). This one's subject is the token
  # exchange itself — validity and expiry — so it hands back the raw
  # session/token record rather than a conn already carrying it.
  def portal_magic_link_fixture(client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, session} = CleanerCrm.Portal.create_portal_session(client, Enum.into(attrs, %{}))
    session
  end

  # Reviews (story 853) — an already-sent review request for a
  # completed visit, distinct from the thank-you/request send itself
  # (covered end-to-end by criteria 7244/7245's own specs). Scenarios
  # whose subject is what happens once the client reaches
  # `ReviewLive.Public` (rating routing, no-duplicate-request) seed
  # the already-requested review directly here instead of re-driving
  # the completion-to-request pipeline every time — a sanctioned
  # shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def review_request_fixture(scope, job, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, review} =
      CleanerCrm.Reviews.create_review(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          client_id: client.id,
          status: :review_requested,
          token: "review_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}",
          review_request_sent_at: DateTime.utc_now()
        })
      )

    review
  end

  # Reviews (story 853) — runs the periodic review-request scan now,
  # exactly as `CleanerCrm.Reviews.ReviewScheduler.perform/1` does on
  # its Oban cron schedule (mirrors `send_due_reminders/0` above for
  # story 837's reminder scan). `as_of` lets a spec assert the
  # ~24h-later trigger without backdating any row's own timestamp —
  # the same injectable "now" seam `ReminderScheduler.scan_and_send/1`
  # already uses.
  def run_due_review_requests(as_of \\ DateTime.utc_now()) do
    CleanerCrm.Reviews.send_due_review_requests(as_of)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Case do
  @moduledoc """
  Base case for spex (BDD spec) tests.

  Wires up Phoenix.ConnTest for HTTP assertions, Phoenix.LiveViewTest
  for driving LiveViews, the SexySpex DSL (spex/scenario/given_/when_/then_),
  and the DB sandbox.

  use ExUnit.CaseTemplate

  using do
    quote do
      @endpoint CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint

      use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes
      use SexySpex

      import Plug.Conn
      import Phoenix.ConnTest
      import Phoenix.LiveViewTest
      import CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  end

  setup tags do

    {:ok, conn: Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn()}
  end
end

=== billing.ex ===
defmodule CleanerCrm.Billing do
  @moduledoc """
  Invoices generated from completed jobs and payment collection via
  card-on-file or a public payment link, with proof-of-work attached
  from `CleanerCrm.Quality` for chargeback defense.

  Per the payments-stripe ADR, an invoice's `status` only ever advances
  on a Stripe webhook confirmation: `charge_card/2` and
  `pay_via_link/2` just submit a PaymentIntent and move the invoice to
  `:charge_pending`; only `receive_webhook/1` marks it `:paid`, or
  reverts it to `:unpaid` on a decline so the owner can retry or send a
  payment link.

  Every function that isn't reached from the public `/pay/:token` or
  `/webhooks/stripe` routes is scoped to the caller's active account —
  those two have no logged-in user to scope against.

  ## Job completion integration point

  No caller generates an invoice automatically yet: job completion
  itself lives in `CleanerCrm.Quality.complete_job/2`
  (`CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.Job`, which will drive it, doesn't exist
  yet either). Once it does, the natural hook is right there — call
  `generate_for_job/2` with the now-completed job after
  `Quality.complete_job/2` succeeds.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Billing.{Invoice, Payment, ReceiptNotifier, StripeGateway}
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  ## Invoices

  @doc "Lists the account's invoices, most recent first, for the billing queue."
  def list_invoices(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Invoice
    |> where([i], i.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([i], desc: i.inserted_at)
    |> preload(job: :client)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_invoice!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Invoice
    |> where([i], i.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload(job: :client)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  @doc """
  Looks up an invoice by its public payment-link token. Takes no
  `Scope` — the payer on `/pay/:token` isn't a logged-in user, so the
  token itself (unguessable, unique) is the only access control this
  lookup has.
  """
  def get_invoice_by_token(token) when is_binary(token) do
    Invoice
    |> where([i], i.payment_token == ^token)
    |> preload(job: :client)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  def create_invoice(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Invoice{account_id: account_id}
    |> Invoice.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Generates the invoice for a job that's just been marked complete —
  see the moduledoc for where this gets wired in once job completion
  has a real caller.

  Returns `{:error, :no_price}` without creating an invoice, and
  without touching the database at all, when the job has no
  `agreed_price_cents` — e.g. a visit materialized from a
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan` with no price set (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence.job_attrs/1`). Job completion itself
  must still succeed in that case, so callers should let this error
  through rather than fail the completion on it. There's no dedicated
  "completed jobs missing an invoice" queue today — the office notices
  a missing invoice by comparing the schedule board's completed jobs
  against `list_invoices/1`, or avoids it entirely by pricing the job
  (or its recurring plan) before it's completed.
  """
  def generate_for_job(%Scope{}, %Job{agreed_price_cents: nil}), do: {:error, :no_price}

  def generate_for_job(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
    create_invoice(scope, %{job_id: job.id, amount_cents: job.agreed_price_cents, status: :unpaid})
  end

  ## Payment collection

  @doc """
  Charges the client's card on file for the invoice's full amount.
  Refused with `{:error, :no_card_on_file}` when the client has none.
  """
  def charge_card(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
        %Invoice{account_id: account_id} = invoice
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    invoice
    |> invoice_client()
    |> submit_and_finalize_charge(invoice, off_session: true, source: "card_on_file")
  end

  defp submit_and_finalize_charge(%Client{card_on_file: false}, _invoice, _opts),
    do: {:error, :no_card_on_file}

  defp submit_and_finalize_charge(%Client{} = client, invoice, opts) do
    {source, charge_opts} = Keyword.pop!(opts, :source)

    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id}} <-
           submit_charge(invoice, payment_method_for(client), charge_opts) do
      finalize_charge_submission(invoice, client, intent_id, source)
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Charges the given payment method against the invoice reached via its
  public payment-link token — the `/pay/:token` page's own flow, with
  no card on file and no logged-in payer to scope against.
  """
  def pay_via_link(%Invoice{} = invoice, payment_method) when is_binary(payment_method) do
    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id}} <- submit_charge(invoice, payment_method, off_session: false) do
      finalize_charge_submission(invoice, invoice_client(invoice), intent_id, "payment_link")
    end
  end

  defp submit_charge(%Invoice{} = invoice, payment_method, opts) do
    StripeGateway.create_payment_intent(%{
      amount_cents: invoice.amount_cents,
      payment_method: payment_method,
      off_session: Keyword.get(opts, :off_session, false),
      metadata: %{invoice_id: invoice.id}
    })
  end

  # Clients doesn't yet persist a real Stripe payment-method/customer id
  # (only the `card_on_file` flag) — this placeholder stands in until a
  # SetupIntent-backed token is stored. The Test adapter ignores it
  # entirely, and the Live adapter is never exercised without one.
  defp payment_method_for(%Client{id: id}), do: "card_on_file:#{id}"

  defp finalize_charge_submission(%Invoice{} = invoice, client, intent_id, source) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, updated} <-
             invoice
             |> Invoice.changeset(%{status: :charge_pending, stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id})
             |> Repo.update(),
           {:ok, _payment} <- record_payment(updated, intent_id, source, :pending) do
        {:ok, updated}
      end
    end)
    |> tap(fn
      {:ok, updated} -> send_receipt(client, updated)
      _error -> :ok
    end)
  end

  @doc """
  Generates (or reuses) an invoice's public payment-link token, so the
  owner can share `/pay/:token` with a client who has no card on file.
  """
  def create_payment_link(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
        %Invoice{account_id: account_id} = invoice
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    invoice
    |> Invoice.changeset(%{payment_token: invoice.payment_token || generate_token()})
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  defp generate_token, do: 16 |> :crypto.strong_rand_bytes() |> Base.url_encode64(padding: false)

  defp invoice_client(%Invoice{} = invoice) do
    invoice |> Repo.preload(job: :client) |> then(& &1.job.client)
  end

  defp send_receipt(%Client{email: email}, %Invoice{} = invoice) when is_binary(email) do
    ReceiptNotifier.deliver_receipt(email, invoice)
    :ok
  end

  defp send_receipt(_client, _invoice), do: :ok

  defp record_payment(%Invoice{} = invoice, intent_id, source, status) do
    %Payment{account_id: invoice.account_id, invoice_id: invoice.id}
    |> Payment.changeset(%{
      amount_cents: invoice.amount_cents,
      status: status,
      provider: "stripe",
      stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id,
      source: source
    })

  @doc """
  Verifies and applies an inbound Stripe webhook request — the
  controller's only touchpoint into this context, so it never sees
  event data it can't trust.

    with {:ok, event} <- StripeGateway.verify_webhook_event(conn) do

    with {:ok, invoice} <- find_invoice_for_event(event) do
      transition_invoice(invoice, :paid, :succeeded)

    end

  defp find_invoice_for_event(%{"data" => %{"object" => object}}) do
    case object do
      %{"metadata" => %{"invoice_id" => invoice_id}} when is_binary(invoice_id) ->
        fetch_invoice(invoice_id)

      %{"id" => intent_id} when is_binary(intent_id) ->
        fetch_invoice_by_intent(intent_id)

      _ ->
        {:error, :invoice_not_found}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_invoice(invoice_id) do
    case Repo.get(Invoice, invoice_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :invoice_not_found}
      invoice -> {:ok, invoice}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_invoice_by_intent(intent_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Invoice, stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :invoice_not_found}
      invoice -> {:ok, invoice}
    end

  # cleared) — its presence is what tells `CleanerCrmWeb.InvoiceLive.Show`
  # to offer "retry" instead of the initial "charge card" action.
  defp transition_invoice(%Invoice{} = invoice, new_status, payment_status) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->

  # `:pending` here and just gets its outcome filled in; a fixture-seeded
  # invoice (no prior `charge_card/2` call) has none, so one is created
  # for the audit trail.

         ) do

    end
  end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Quoting do
  @moduledoc """
  Quotes built from the account's rate card using per-room, per-sqft,
  or hourly pricing models.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account. A quote is
  built up in memory (see `CleanerCrm.Quoting.Pricing`) and only ever
  persisted at the moment it's sent — `send_quote/3` freezes the rate
  card's current rates into the quote's line items, so later rate-card
  edits never alter an already-sent quote.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting.{Quote, QuoteItem, RateCard, Pricing}

  ## Rate card

  @doc """
  Returns the account's rate card, creating a blank one on first use.
  """
  def get_or_create_rate_card(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(RateCard, account_id: account_id) do
      nil -> Repo.insert!(%RateCard{account_id: account_id})
      rate_card -> rate_card
    end
  end

  def change_rate_card(%Scope{}, %RateCard{} = rate_card, attrs \\ %{}) do
    RateCard.changeset(rate_card, attrs)
  end

  def update_rate_card(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %RateCard{} = rate_card, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    rate_card
    |> RateCard.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  ## Quotes

  def change_quote(%Scope{}, %Quote{} = quote, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Quote.changeset(quote, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Lists the account's quotes, most recently sent first.
  """
  def list_quotes(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Quote
    |> where([q], q.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([q], desc: q.inserted_at)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_quote!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Quote
    |> where([q], q.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload(:quote_items)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  @doc """
  Finalizes a draft quote against the current rate card: prices every
  line item, then inserts the quote and its `CleanerCrm.Quoting.QuoteItem`s
  together, freezing the rates and amounts at this moment.

  Refuses with `{:error, :not_finalizable}` when any priced line item
  is missing a rate on the rate card, or the total isn't positive — a
  sent quote can never be a zero-dollar or partially-rated quote.
  """
  def send_quote(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope,
        %Quote{} = draft,
        %RateCard{} = rate_card
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    line_items = Pricing.line_items(rate_card, draft)

    if Pricing.finalizable?(line_items) do
      insert_sent_quote(scope, account_id, draft, line_items)
    else
      {:error, :not_finalizable}
    end
  end

  defp insert_sent_quote(scope, account_id, draft, line_items) do
    quote_attrs = %{
      client_id: draft.client_id,
      client_name: draft.client_name,
      client_phone: draft.client_phone,
      pricing_model: draft.pricing_model,
      bedroom_count: draft.bedroom_count,
      bathroom_count: draft.bathroom_count,
      square_feet: draft.square_feet,
      hours: draft.hours,
      status: :sent,
      total_cents: Pricing.total_cents(line_items),
      sent_at: DateTime.utc_now()
    }

    Repo.transaction(fn ->
      with {:ok, quote} <-
             %Quote{account_id: account_id} |> Quote.changeset(quote_attrs) |> Repo.insert(),
           {:ok, _items} <- insert_quote_items(quote, line_items) do
        Recorder.record(scope, "quote_sent", "Quote", quote.id, %{}, %{
          "total_cents" => quote.total_cents
        })

        quote
      else
        {:error, changeset} -> Repo.rollback(changeset)
      end
    end)
  end

  defp insert_quote_items(quote, line_items) do
    Enum.reduce_while(line_items, {:ok, []}, fn line_item, {:ok, acc} ->
      case %QuoteItem{quote_id: quote.id} |> QuoteItem.changeset(line_item) |> Repo.insert() do
        {:ok, quote_item} -> {:cont, {:ok, [quote_item | acc]}}
        {:error, _changeset} = error -> {:halt, error}
      end
    end)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Billing do
  @moduledoc """
  Invoices generated from completed jobs and payment collection via
  card-on-file or a public payment link, with proof-of-work attached
  from `CleanerCrm.Quality` for chargeback defense.

  Per the payments-stripe ADR, an invoice's `status` only ever advances
  on a Stripe webhook confirmation: `charge_card/2` and
  `pay_via_link/2` just submit a PaymentIntent and move the invoice to
  `:charge_pending`; only `receive_webhook/1` marks it `:paid`, or
  reverts it to `:unpaid` on a decline so the owner can retry or send a
  payment link.

  Every function that isn't reached from the public `/pay/:token` or
  `/webhooks/stripe` routes is scoped to the caller's active account —
  those two have no logged-in user to scope against.

  ## Job completion integration point

  No caller generates an invoice automatically yet: job completion
  itself lives in `CleanerCrm.Quality.complete_job/2`
  (`CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.Job`, which will drive it, doesn't exist
  yet either). Once it does, the natural hook is right there — call
  `generate_for_job/2` with the now-completed job after
  `Quality.complete_job/2` succeeds.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Billing.{Invoice, Payment, ReceiptNotifier, StripeGateway}
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  ## Invoices

  @doc "Lists the account's invoices, most recent first, for the billing queue."
  def list_invoices(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Invoice
    |> where([i], i.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([i], desc: i.inserted_at)
    |> preload(job: :client)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_invoice!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Invoice
    |> where([i], i.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload(job: :client)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  @doc """
  Looks up an invoice by its public payment-link token. Takes no
  `Scope` — the payer on `/pay/:token` isn't a logged-in user, so the
  token itself (unguessable, unique) is the only access control this
  lookup has.
  """
  def get_invoice_by_token(token) when is_binary(token) do
    Invoice
    |> where([i], i.payment_token == ^token)
    |> preload(job: :client)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  def create_invoice(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Invoice{account_id: account_id}
    |> Invoice.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Generates the invoice for a job that's just been marked complete —
  see the moduledoc for where this gets wired in once job completion
  has a real caller.

  Returns `{:error, :no_price}` without creating an invoice, and
  without touching the database at all, when the job has no
  `agreed_price_cents` — e.g. a visit materialized from a
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan` with no price set (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence.job_attrs/1`). Job completion itself
  must still succeed in that case, so callers should let this error
  through rather than fail the completion on it. There's no dedicated
  "completed jobs missing an invoice" queue today — the office notices
  a missing invoice by comparing the schedule board's completed jobs
  against `list_invoices/1`, or avoids it entirely by pricing the job
  (or its recurring plan) before it's completed.
  """
  def generate_for_job(%Scope{}, %Job{agreed_price_cents: nil}), do: {:error, :no_price}

  def generate_for_job(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
    create_invoice(scope, %{job_id: job.id, amount_cents: job.agreed_price_cents, status: :unpaid})
  end

  ## Payment collection

  @doc """
  Charges the client's card on file for the invoice's full amount.
  Refused with `{:error, :no_card_on_file}` when the client has none.
  """
  def charge_card(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
        %Invoice{account_id: account_id} = invoice
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    invoice
    |> invoice_client()
    |> submit_and_finalize_charge(invoice, off_session: true, source: "card_on_file")
  end

  defp submit_and_finalize_charge(%Client{card_on_file: false}, _invoice, _opts),
    do: {:error, :no_card_on_file}

  defp submit_and_finalize_charge(%Client{} = client, invoice, opts) do
    {source, charge_opts} = Keyword.pop!(opts, :source)

    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id}} <-
           submit_charge(invoice, payment_method_for(client), charge_opts) do
      finalize_charge_submission(invoice, client, intent_id, source)
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Charges the given payment method against the invoice reached via its
  public payment-link token — the `/pay/:token` page's own flow, with
  no card on file and no logged-in payer to scope against.
  """
  def pay_via_link(%Invoice{} = invoice, payment_method) when is_binary(payment_method) do
    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id}} <- submit_charge(invoice, payment_method, off_session: false) do
      finalize_charge_submission(invoice, invoice_client(invoice), intent_id, "payment_link")
    end
  end

  defp submit_charge(%Invoice{} = invoice, payment_method, opts) do
    StripeGateway.create_payment_intent(%{
      amount_cents: invoice.amount_cents,
      payment_method: payment_method,
      off_session: Keyword.get(opts, :off_session, false),
      metadata: %{invoice_id: invoice.id}
    })
  end

  # Clients doesn't yet persist a real Stripe payment-method/customer id
  # (only the `card_on_file` flag) — this placeholder stands in until a
  # SetupIntent-backed token is stored. The Test adapter ignores it
  # entirely, and the Live adapter is never exercised without one.
  defp payment_method_for(%Client{id: id}), do: "card_on_file:#{id}"

  defp finalize_charge_submission(%Invoice{} = invoice, client, intent_id, source) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, updated} <-
             invoice
             |> Invoice.changeset(%{status: :charge_pending, stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id})
             |> Repo.update(),
           {:ok, _payment} <- record_payment(updated, intent_id, source, :pending) do
        {:ok, updated}
      end
    end)
    |> tap(fn
      {:ok, updated} -> send_receipt(client, updated)
      _error -> :ok
    end)
  end

  @doc """
  Generates (or reuses) an invoice's public payment-link token, so the
  owner can share `/pay/:token` with a client who has no card on file.
  """
  def create_payment_link(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
        %Invoice{account_id: account_id} = invoice
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    invoice
    |> Invoice.changeset(%{payment_token: invoice.payment_token || generate_token()})
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  defp generate_token, do: 16 |> :crypto.strong_rand_bytes() |> Base.url_encode64(padding: false)

  defp invoice_client(%Invoice{} = invoice) do
    invoice |> Repo.preload(job: :client) |> then(& &1.job.client)
  end

  defp send_receipt(%Client{email: email}, %Invoice{} = invoice) when is_binary(email) do
    ReceiptNotifier.deliver_receipt(email, invoice)
    :ok
  end

  defp send_receipt(_client, _invoice), do: :ok

  defp record_payment(%Invoice{} = invoice, intent_id, source, status) do
    %Payment{account_id: invoice.account_id, invoice_id: invoice.id}
    |> Payment.changeset(%{
      amount_cents: invoice.amount_cents,
      status: status,
      provider: "stripe",
      stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id,
      source: source
    })
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Webhook

  @doc """
  Verifies and applies an inbound Stripe webhook request — the
  controller's only touchpoint into this context, so it never sees
  event data it can't trust.
  """
  def receive_webhook(conn) do
    with {:ok, event} <- StripeGateway.verify_webhook_event(conn) do
      apply_webhook_event(event)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.succeeded"} = event) do
    with {:ok, invoice} <- find_invoice_for_event(event) do
      transition_invoice(invoice, :paid, :succeeded)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.payment_failed"} = event) do
    with {:ok, invoice} <- find_invoice_for_event(event) do
      transition_invoice(invoice, :unpaid, :failed)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => _other}), do: {:ok, :ignored}

  defp find_invoice_for_event(%{"data" => %{"object" => object}}) do
    case object do
      %{"metadata" => %{"invoice_id" => invoice_id}} when is_binary(invoice_id) ->
        fetch_invoice(invoice_id)

      %{"id" => intent_id} when is_binary(intent_id) ->
        fetch_invoice_by_intent(intent_id)

      _ ->
        {:error, :invoice_not_found}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_invoice(invoice_id) do
    case Repo.get(Invoice, invoice_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :invoice_not_found}
      invoice -> {:ok, invoice}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_invoice_by_intent(intent_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Invoice, stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :invoice_not_found}
      invoice -> {:ok, invoice}
    end
  end

  # `stripe_payment_intent_id` is left as-is on a decline (never
  # cleared) — its presence is what tells `CleanerCrmWeb.InvoiceLive.Show`
  # to offer "retry" instead of the initial "charge card" action.
  defp transition_invoice(%Invoice{} = invoice, new_status, payment_status) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, updated} <- invoice |> Invoice.changeset(%{status: new_status}) |> Repo.update() do
        update_payment_record(updated, payment_status)
        {:ok, updated}
      end
    end)
  end

  # The `Payment` submitted alongside the charge is normally still
  # `:pending` here and just gets its outcome filled in; a fixture-seeded
  # invoice (no prior `charge_card/2` call) has none, so one is created
  # for the audit trail.
  defp update_payment_record(%Invoice{} = invoice, status) do
    case Repo.get_by(Payment,
           invoice_id: invoice.id,
           stripe_payment_intent_id: invoice.stripe_payment_intent_id
         ) do
      nil -> record_payment(invoice, invoice.stripe_payment_intent_id, "webhook", status)
      payment -> payment |> Payment.changeset(%{status: status}) |> Repo.update()

defmodule CleanerCrm.Quoting.RateCard do
  @moduledoc """
  The account's configurable rates, one per pricing model.

  A single row per account (see `CleanerCrm.Quoting.get_or_create_rate_card/1`).
  A rate left blank means that pricing model isn't priced yet — quoting
  against it is refused until the owner sets a rate (see
  `CleanerCrm.Quoting.Pricing`).

defmodule CleanerCrm.Quoting.Pricing do
  @moduledoc """
  Computes a quote's line items and total from a rate card, and decides
  whether a quote is ready to send.

  Pure and side-effect free: it never touches the database, so
  `CleanerCrmWeb.QuoteLive.Builder` can call it on every keystroke for
  live totals, and `CleanerCrm.Quoting.send_quote/3` can call it again
  at the moment of persistence.

  Per the money-handling ADR, rate math is done in `Decimal` and
  rounded half-up to whole cents.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting.{Quote, RateCard}

  @type line_item :: %{
          description: String.t(),
          quantity: integer(),
          rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          amount_cents: integer()
        }

  @doc """
  The quote form field names (as submitted param keys) that belong to
  a given pricing model — used to drop inputs left over from a
  previously selected model when the owner switches models.
  """
  @spec fields_for_model(String.t()) :: [String.t()]
  def fields_for_model("per_room"), do: ~w(bedroom_count bathroom_count)
  def fields_for_model("per_sqft"), do: ~w(square_feet)
  def fields_for_model("hourly"), do: ~w(hours)
  def fields_for_model(_other), do: []

  @doc """
  The priced line items for a quote's chosen model. Only items with a
  positive quantity are included — an empty or zero field never
  demands a rate. A `nil` `rate_cents` means the rate card has nothing
  configured yet for that item, and its amount is zero.
  """
  @spec line_items(RateCard.t(), Quote.t()) :: [line_item()]
  def line_items(%RateCard{} = rate_card, %Quote{} = quote) do
    quote.pricing_model
    |> model_items(rate_card, quote)
    |> Enum.filter(&(&1.quantity > 0))
  end

  defp model_items(:per_room, rate_card, quote) do
    [
      item("Bedrooms", quote.bedroom_count, rate_card.per_room_bedroom_rate_cents),
      item("Bathrooms", quote.bathroom_count, rate_card.per_room_bathroom_rate_cents)
    ]
  end

  defp model_items(:per_sqft, rate_card, quote) do
    [item("Square footage", quote.square_feet, rate_card.per_sqft_rate_cents)]
  end

  defp model_items(:hourly, rate_card, quote) do
    [item("Hours", quote.hours, rate_card.hourly_rate_cents)]
  end

  defp model_items(nil, _rate_card, _quote), do: []

  defp item(description, quantity, rate_cents) do
    quantity = quantity || 0

    %{
      description: description,
      quantity: quantity,
      rate_cents: rate_cents,
      amount_cents: amount_cents(quantity, rate_cents)
    }
  end

  defp amount_cents(quantity, rate_cents)
       when is_integer(quantity) and is_integer(rate_cents) and quantity > 0 do
    quantity
    |> Decimal.new()
    |> Decimal.mult(Decimal.new(rate_cents))
    |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up)
    |> Decimal.to_integer()
  end

  defp amount_cents(_quantity, _rate_cents), do: 0

  @doc "Sums a quote's line items into its total, in cents."
  @spec total_cents([line_item()]) :: integer()
  def total_cents(line_items), do: Enum.reduce(line_items, 0, &(&1.amount_cents + &2))

  @doc "Whether any priced line item is missing a rate from the rate card."
  @spec missing_rate?([line_item()]) :: boolean()
  def missing_rate?(line_items), do: Enum.any?(line_items, &is_nil(&1.rate_cents))

  @doc """
  Whether a quote is ready to send: at least one priced line item,
  every one of them rated, and a positive total.
  """
  @spec finalizable?([line_item()]) :: boolean()
  def finalizable?(line_items) do
    line_items != [] and not missing_rate?(line_items) and total_cents(line_items) > 0
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway do
  @moduledoc """
  Hides the Stripe API behind two operations: submitting a charge as a
  PaymentIntent, and verifying an inbound webhook request. `CleanerCrm.Billing`
  calls through the configured adapter — `Test` in test (see
  `config/test.exs`), `Live` everywhere else — so a test never reaches
  the real Stripe API, and the real adapter is the only one that ever
  checks a webhook signature.

  Configure the adapter and (for `Live`) credentials with:

      config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway,
        adapter: CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway.Live,
        secret_key: System.get_env("STRIPE_SECRET_KEY"),
        webhook_secret: System.get_env("STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET")
  """

  @type charge_params :: %{
          required(:amount_cents) => pos_integer(),
          required(:payment_method) => String.t(),
          optional(:off_session) => boolean(),
          optional(:metadata) => map()
        }

  @callback create_payment_intent(charge_params()) ::
              {:ok, %{id: String.t(), status: String.t()}} | {:error, map()}

  @callback verify_webhook_event(Plug.Conn.t()) :: {:ok, map()} | {:error, atom()}

  def create_payment_intent(params), do: adapter().create_payment_intent(params)

  def verify_webhook_event(conn), do: adapter().verify_webhook_event(conn)

  defp adapter do
    :cleaner_crm
    |> Application.get_env(__MODULE__, [])
    |> Keyword.get(:adapter, __MODULE__.Live)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway.Test do
  @moduledoc """
  Deterministic in-memory stand-in for Stripe, configured as the
  adapter for `CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway` in `config/test.exs`.
  Every charge submits successfully — declines in this app are only
  ever driven by the webhook the spec posts directly to
  `POST /webhooks/stripe`, never by this adapter — and the webhook
  event is trusted as-is, since nothing in test ever signs one.
  """

  @behaviour CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway

  @impl true
  def create_payment_intent(_params) do
    {:ok, %{id: "pi_test_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}", status: "succeeded"}}
  end

  @impl true
  def verify_webhook_event(conn), do: {:ok, conn.params}

defmodule CleanerCrm.Billing.Invoice do
  @moduledoc """
  An invoice for a completed job.

  Per the payments-stripe ADR, `status` only ever advances on a Stripe
  webhook confirmation: charging a card or sending a payment link just
  submits a charge and moves the invoice to `:charge_pending`; only the
  webhook marks it `:paid`, and a declined charge reverts it to
  `:unpaid` so the owner can retry or fall back to a payment link.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type status :: :unpaid | :charge_pending | :paid

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          job_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          amount_cents: integer() | nil,
          status: status(),
          stripe_payment_intent_id: String.t() | nil,
          payment_token: String.t() | nil,
          job: CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job.t() | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "invoices" do
    field :amount_cents, :integer
    field :amount, :decimal, virtual: true
    field :status, Ecto.Enum, values: [:unpaid, :charge_pending, :paid], default: :unpaid
    field :stripe_payment_intent_id, :string
    field :payment_token, :string

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :job, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(job_id amount amount_cents status stripe_payment_intent_id payment_token)a

  def changeset(invoice, attrs) do
    invoice
    |> cast(attrs, @fields)
    |> validate_required([:job_id])
    |> put_amount_cents()
    # After `put_amount_cents/1`, not before — a caller supplying dollars
    # via `amount` has no `amount_cents` yet until that step runs.
    # Needed because `validate_number/3` below only runs against an
    # actual *change*, so an explicit `amount_cents: nil` (unchanged from
    # a fresh `%Invoice{}`'s own default) silently skips it and would
    # otherwise reach `amount_cents`'s NOT NULL column as a raised
    # constraint violation instead of a changeset error.
    |> validate_required([:amount_cents])
    |> validate_number(:amount_cents, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> unique_constraint(:payment_token)
  end

  # `amount` arrives as dollars (a `Decimal`, matching the money-handling
  # ADR); rounded half-up and stored as `amount_cents` — the only column
  # ever persisted. Callers that already have cents (e.g. copying a job's
  # `agreed_price_cents`) pass `amount_cents` directly and skip this.
  defp put_amount_cents(changeset) do
    case get_change(changeset, :amount) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      %Decimal{} = amount ->
        cents = amount |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer()
        put_change(changeset, :amount_cents, cents)
    end
  end
end

=== clients.ex ===
defmodule CleanerCrm.Clients do
  @moduledoc """
  Clients and their properties: addresses, parking notes, entry
  methods and codes, pets, and cleaning preferences — the authoritative
  access and scope record every job carries.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.{Client, Property}
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder

  ## Clients

  def list_clients(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Client
    |> where([c], c.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([c], asc: c.name)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_client!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Client
    |> where([c], c.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def create_client(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Client{account_id: account_id}
    |> Client.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  def change_client(%Scope{}, %Client{} = client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Client.changeset(client, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Lists only active clients, for the account's day-to-day client list.
  """
  def list_active_clients(%Scope{} = scope) do
    scope |> list_clients() |> Enum.filter(& &1.active)
  end

  def update_client(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Client{} = client, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    client
    |> Client.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  def deactivate_client(%Scope{} = scope, %Client{} = client) do
    update_client(scope, client, %{"active" => false})
  end

  def reactivate_client(%Scope{} = scope, %Client{} = client) do
    update_client(scope, client, %{"active" => true})
  end

  @doc """
  Permanently deletes a client and its properties.

  Refuses to delete a client that still has dependent records (e.g.
  scheduled jobs) elsewhere in the system — the database's foreign key
  constraints are the source of truth for what's "dependent," so this
  context stays ignorant of any other bounded context's schema.
  """
  def delete_client(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Client{} = client)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.delete(client)
  rescue
    Ecto.ConstraintError -> {:error, :has_upcoming_jobs}
  end

  ## Properties

  @doc """
  Lists a client's properties, ordered by address.
  """
  def list_properties(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Client{id: client_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Property
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id and p.client_id == ^client_id)
    |> order_by([p], asc: p.service_address)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_property!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Property
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def create_property(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Property{account_id: account_id}
    |> Property.changeset(attrs)
    |> validate_client_ownership(scope)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Updates a property. When entry method, lockbox code, or alarm code
  change, records an audit entry naming the changed fields (never the
  code values themselves).
  """
  def update_property(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope,
        %Property{} = property,
        attrs
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    changeset =
      property
      |> Property.changeset(attrs)
      |> validate_client_ownership(scope)

    with {:ok, updated} <- Repo.update(changeset) do
      record_access_code_changes(scope, changeset, updated.id)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def change_property(%Scope{}, %Property{} = property, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Property.changeset(property, attrs)
  end

  defp validate_client_ownership(changeset, %Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) do
    case Ecto.Changeset.get_change(changeset, :client_id) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      client_id ->
        query = where(Client, [c], c.id == ^client_id and c.account_id == ^account_id)

        if Repo.exists?(query) do
          changeset
        else
          Ecto.Changeset.add_error(changeset, :client_id, "is invalid")
        end
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Lists audit entries recorded against a property, most recent first.
  """
  def list_property_audit_entries(%Scope{} = scope, %Property{} = property) do
    Recorder.list_for_subject(scope, "Property", property.id)
  end

  defp record_access_code_changes(scope, changeset, property_id) do
    changed_fields =
      Property.access_code_fields()
      |> Enum.filter(&Ecto.Changeset.get_change(changeset, &1))
      |> Enum.map(&to_string/1)

    case changed_fields do
      [] ->
        :ok

      fields ->
        Recorder.record(scope, "access_details_updated", "Property", property_id, %{}, %{
          "changed_fields" => fields
        })
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling do
  @moduledoc """
  Recurring plans and the jobs they generate, cleaner time-off, and
  conflict-aware assignment.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Property
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{
    AvailabilityBlock,
    ConflictDetector,
    Job,
    Recurrence,
    RecurringPlan
  }

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

    scope
    |> list_cleaners()
    |> Enum.find(&(&1.id == cleaner_id))
    |> case do

      cleaner -> cleaner
    end
  end

      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    cleaner_id = parse_cleaner_id(cleaner_id)

    AvailabilityBlock
    |> where([b], b.account_id == ^account_id and b.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id)
    |> order_by([b], asc: b.date)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  Lists a cleaner's upcoming (today or later, non-cancelled) jobs for
  their detail page, soonest first.
  """
  def list_upcoming_jobs_for_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    cleaner_id = parse_cleaner_id(cleaner_id)

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and
        j.status != :cancelled and j.scheduled_date >= ^Date.utc_today()
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  defp parse_cleaner_id(id) when is_integer(id), do: id
  defp parse_cleaner_id(id) when is_binary(id), do: String.to_integer(id)

  defp insert_cleaner_user(name) do
    %User{}
    |> Ecto.Changeset.cast(%{name: name, email: placeholder_email(name)}, [:name, :email])
    |> Ecto.Changeset.validate_required([:name, :email])
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp placeholder_email(name) do
    slug =
      name
      |> String.downcase()
      |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]+/, ".")
      |> String.trim(".")

    "#{slug}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@cleaners.local"
  end
end

  defp audit_value(%Date{} = value), do: to_string(value)
  defp audit_value(%Time{} = value), do: to_string(value)
  defp audit_value(value), do: value

  @doc """
  Removes a job from the board without hard-deleting its row — the
  row (and any audit entries already about it) stays resolvable for
  the trail. Distinct from `cancel_job/2`: this is the office
  correcting a mistaken entry rather than calling off an appointment,
  so it's recorded as "deleted" rather than "cancelled" and never
  notifies the assigned cleaner.
  """
  def delete_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_deleted",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  ## Recurring plans

  def get_recurring_plan!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    RecurringPlan
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:property, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_recurring_plan(%Scope{}, %RecurringPlan{} = plan, attrs \\ %{}) do
    RecurringPlan.preview_changeset(plan, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Runs conflict detection for a (possibly unsaved) plan's full series
  against its preferred cleaner, without persisting anything. Returns
  only the conflicting occurrences, as `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
  """
  def preview_conflicts(scope, %RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
    ConflictDetector.check_occurrences(scope, plan, Recurrence.occurrences(plan))
  end

  @doc """
  Saves a recurring plan and materializes its full series of jobs.
  Conflicting occurrences are still created and still assigned to the
  preferred cleaner — conflicts are for the owner to review and
  resolve, never a silent block on saving.
  """
  def create_recurring_plan(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, plan} <-
             %RecurringPlan{account_id: account_id}
             |> RecurringPlan.changeset(attrs)
             |> Repo.insert() do
        jobs =
          plan
          |> Recurrence.job_attrs()
          |> Enum.map(fn job_attrs ->
            {:ok, job} = create_job(scope, job_attrs, actor: :system)
            job
          end)

        {:ok, {plan, jobs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  ## Availability blocks

  def change_availability_block(%Scope{}, %AvailabilityBlock{} = block, attrs \\ %{}) do
    AvailabilityBlock.changeset(block, attrs)
  end

  def create_availability_block(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %AvailabilityBlock{account_id: account_id}
    |> AvailabilityBlock.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Cleaners (account members who take jobs)

  @doc """
  Lists the account's members as candidate cleaners for the board and
  assignment pickers.
  """
  def list_cleaners(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> Accounts.list_account_members(account_id)
    |> Enum.map(& &1.user)
  end

  @doc """
  Registers a new cleaner: a user identified by display name (rather
  than login credentials) added to the account as a member, so jobs
  and availability can be assigned to them. There is no login flow for
  a cleaner created this way — see `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3`
  for the (real, login-capable) path other stories seed cleaners
  through.
  """
  def register_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, name)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(name) do
    with {:ok, user} <- insert_cleaner_user(name),
         {:ok, _member} <- Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account_id, :member) do
      {:ok, user}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Fetches a single cleaner by id, for their detail page. Draws from
  the same membership list as `list_cleaners/1`, so a user who isn't
  a member of this account can't be looked up here either. Raises if
  not found.
  """
  def get_cleaner!(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
    cleaner_id = parse_cleaner_id(id)

    scope
    |> list_cleaners()
    |> Enum.find(&(&1.id == cleaner_id))
    |> case do
      nil -> raise Ecto.NoResultsError, queryable: User
      cleaner -> cleaner
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Lists a cleaner's time-off blocks for their detail page, soonest
  first.
  """
  def list_availability_blocks(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    cleaner_id = parse_cleaner_id(cleaner_id)

    AvailabilityBlock
    |> where([b], b.account_id == ^account_id and b.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id)
    |> order_by([b], asc: b.date)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists a cleaner's upcoming (today or later, non-cancelled) jobs for
  their detail page, soonest first.
  """
  def list_upcoming_jobs_for_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    cleaner_id = parse_cleaner_id(cleaner_id)

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and
        j.status != :cancelled and j.scheduled_date >= ^Date.utc_today()
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  defp parse_cleaner_id(id) when is_integer(id), do: id
  defp parse_cleaner_id(id) when is_binary(id), do: String.to_integer(id)

  defp insert_cleaner_user(name) do
    %User{}
    |> Ecto.Changeset.cast(%{name: name, email: placeholder_email(name)}, [:name, :email])
    |> Ecto.Changeset.validate_required([:name, :email])
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp placeholder_email(name) do
    slug =
      name
      |> String.downcase()
      |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]+/, ".")
      |> String.trim(".")

    "#{slug}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@cleaners.local"
  end
end
