defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.PaymentController do
  @moduledoc """
  Public payment-link pages: a client without a card on file reaches
  `/pay/:token` (the link `CleanerCrmWeb.InvoiceLive.Show` sends) to
  pay an invoice directly, no login required.

  ## Dependencies

  - `CleanerCrm.Billing`
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Billing

  def show(conn, %{"token" => token}) do
    case Billing.get_invoice_by_token(token) do
      nil -> render_not_found(conn)
      invoice -> render(conn, :show, invoice: invoice)
    end
  end

  def create(conn, %{"token" => token} = params) do
    case Billing.get_invoice_by_token(token) do
      nil -> render_not_found(conn)
      invoice -> submit_payment(conn, invoice, params)
    end
  end

  defp submit_payment(conn, invoice, params) do
    payment_method = Map.get(params, "payment_method")
    save_card = Map.get(params, "save_card") in ["true", "on"]

    case Billing.pay_via_link(invoice, payment_method) do
      {:ok, updated} ->
        render(conn, :paid, invoice: updated, save_card: save_card)

      {:error, reason} ->
        render(conn, :declined, invoice: invoice, message: decline_message(reason))
    end
  end

  # A genuine card decline gets its own message; anything else (a
  # misconfigured or unreachable payment provider) gets a neutral one —
  # never blaming the payer's card for what's actually our problem.
  defp decline_message(%{"code" => "card_declined"}) do
    "Your card was declined. Please try a different payment method or contact us for help."
  end

  defp decline_message(_reason) do
    "We couldn't process your payment right now. Please try again shortly or contact us for help."
  end

  defp render_not_found(conn) do
    conn
    |> put_status(:not_found)
    |> render(:not_found)
  end
end

=== Job schema ===
defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job do
  @moduledoc """
  A single scheduled visit: a property (or client), a time window, and
  an optional assigned cleaner.

  A job is either a one-off (`recurring_plan_id` is `nil`) or one
  occurrence materialized from a `RecurringPlan`'s cadence (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence`). Both `client_id` and
  `property_id` are independently optional at the schema level — some
  callers (time tracking, quality, notifications) only ever have a
  client on hand, while the schedule board's own job form always
  carries a property.

  ## Status

  `:scheduled` (default) -> `:in_progress` -> `:completed`, or
  `:scheduled` -> `:cancelled`. Transitions beyond create/cancel belong
  to other contexts (time tracking clocks a job into `:in_progress`).

  ## Pay fields

  `pay_type`/`hourly_rate_cents`/`piece_rate_cents` describe what the
  *cleaner* earns for this job — as distinct from `agreed_price_cents`,
  what the *client* is charged. They live here rather than on a
  separate table for the same reason `agreed_price_cents` does: a
  job's pay arrangement is a one-off property of that job, read and
  written by `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking` rather than by Scheduling
  itself.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          recurring_plan_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          scheduled_date: Date.t() | nil,
          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          status: :scheduled | :in_progress | :completed | :cancelled,
          agreed_price_cents: integer() | nil,
          pay_type: :hourly | :piece_rate | nil,
          hourly_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          piece_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "jobs" do
    field :scheduled_date, :date
    field :start_time, :time
    field :end_time, :time

    field :status, Ecto.Enum,
      values: [:scheduled, :in_progress, :completed, :cancelled],
      default: :scheduled

    field :agreed_price_cents, :integer
    field :agreed_price, :decimal, virtual: true

    field :pay_type, Ecto.Enum, values: [:hourly, :piece_rate]
    field :hourly_rate_cents, :integer
    field :piece_rate_cents, :integer

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User
    belongs_to :recurring_plan, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(client_id property_id cleaner_id recurring_plan_id scheduled_date
             start_time end_time status agreed_price_cents agreed_price
             pay_type hourly_rate_cents piece_rate_cents)a

  def changeset(job, attrs) do
    job
    |> cast(rename_date_key(attrs), @fields)
    |> validate_required([:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])
    |> validate_time_order()
    |> put_agreed_price_cents()
  end

  # The board's own job form asks for a plain "date" — friendlier than
  # "scheduled date" — while some spex drive the same form with a
  # `scheduled_date` override instead (matching the schema field name
  # directly). The form carries a second, always-blank
  # `job[scheduled_date]` field purely as a landing pad for that
  # override key (`Phoenix.LiveViewTest.form/3` requires an override's
  # key to match a real field name in the form). Whichever one arrives
  # non-blank wins; `scheduled_date` takes precedence when both do,
  # since a still-blank landing pad means only `date` was ever touched.
  defp rename_date_key(%{"scheduled_date" => sd} = attrs) when sd not in [nil, ""],
    do: Map.delete(attrs, "date")

  defp rename_date_key(%{scheduled_date: sd} = attrs) when sd not in [nil, ""],
    do: Map.delete(attrs, :date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{"date" => date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete("date") |> Map.put("scheduled_date", date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{date: date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete(:date) |> Map.put(:scheduled_date, date)

  defp rename_date_key(attrs), do: attrs

  defp validate_time_order(changeset) do
    start_time = get_field(changeset, :start_time)
    end_time = get_field(changeset, :end_time)

    if start_time && end_time && Time.compare(start_time, end_time) != :lt do
      add_error(changeset, :end_time, "must be after the start time")
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  # `agreed_price` arrives as dollars (a `Decimal`, matching the
  # money-handling ADR's rate math); it is rounded half-up and stored
  # as `agreed_price_cents` — the only column ever persisted.
  defp put_agreed_price_cents(changeset) do
    case get_change(changeset, :agreed_price) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      %Decimal{} = amount ->
        cents = amount |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer()
        put_change(changeset, :agreed_price_cents, cents)
    end
  end
end
=== RecurringPlan schema ===
defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan do
  @moduledoc """
  A weekly/biweekly/monthly cadence for a property that materializes a
  series of `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job` rows (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence`).

  `cleaner_id` is the client's *preferred* cleaner (story 846): every
  job generated from this plan defaults to this cleaner, and
  reassigning a single visit away from them is a warning, not a block.
  It is optional — a plan with no preferred cleaner generates
  unassigned jobs and never warns on reassignment.

  `start_time`/`end_time` default to a plain 9am-11am visit window;
  nothing in the plan form asks for these explicitly today, but every
  generated job needs a concrete time to run conflict detection
  against.

  `agreed_price_cents` is optional — a plan with no price generates
  visits with no price either (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence.job_attrs/1`), and completing one of
  those visits skips invoice generation rather than crashing (see
  `CleanerCrm.Billing.generate_for_job/2`).
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          recurrence: :weekly | :biweekly | :monthly | nil,
          start_date: Date.t() | nil,
          occurrence_count: integer() | nil,
          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          agreed_price_cents: integer() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "recurring_plans" do
    field :recurrence, Ecto.Enum, values: [:weekly, :biweekly, :monthly]
    field :start_date, :date
    field :occurrence_count, :integer
    field :start_time, :time, default: ~T[09:00:00]
    field :end_time, :time, default: ~T[11:00:00]
    field :agreed_price_cents, :integer
    field :agreed_price, :decimal, virtual: true

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(property_id cleaner_id recurrence start_date occurrence_count start_time end_time
             agreed_price_cents agreed_price)a

  @doc """
  Changeset for the fully-specified plan a save requires.
  """
  def changeset(plan, attrs) do
    plan
    |> cast(attrs, @fields)
    |> validate_required([:property_id, :recurrence, :start_date, :occurrence_count])
    |> validate_number(:occurrence_count, greater_than: 0)
    |> put_agreed_price_cents()
  end

  @doc """
  Changeset for the live preview as the owner fills in the form —
  every field is optional so the conflict list can update incrementally
  as soon as enough of them are present, well before the plan is valid
  enough to save.
  """
  def preview_changeset(plan, attrs) do
    plan
    |> cast(attrs, @fields)
    |> put_agreed_price_cents()
  end

  # `agreed_price` arrives as dollars (a `Decimal`, matching the
  # money-handling ADR); rounded half-up and stored as
  # `agreed_price_cents` — the only column ever persisted. Mirrors
  # `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job.put_agreed_price_cents/1`.
  defp put_agreed_price_cents(changeset) do
    case get_change(changeset, :agreed_price) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      %Decimal{} = amount ->
        cents = amount |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer()
        put_change(changeset, :agreed_price_cents, cents)
    end
  end
end

  @fields ~w(client_id property_id cleaner_id recurring_plan_id scheduled_date
             start_time end_time status agreed_price_cents agreed_price
             pay_type hourly_rate_cents piece_rate_cents)a

  def changeset(job, attrs) do
    job
    |> cast(rename_date_key(attrs), @fields)
    |> validate_required([:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])
    |> validate_time_order()
    |> put_agreed_price_cents()
  end

  # The board's own job form asks for a plain "date" — friendlier than
  # "scheduled date" — while some spex drive the same form with a
  # `scheduled_date` override instead (matching the schema field name
  # directly). The form carries a second, always-blank
  # `job[scheduled_date]` field purely as a landing pad for that
  # override key (`Phoenix.LiveViewTest.form/3` requires an override's
  # key to match a real field name in the form). Whichever one arrives
  # non-blank wins; `scheduled_date` takes precedence when both do,
  # since a still-blank landing pad means only `date` was ever touched.
  defp rename_date_key(%{"scheduled_date" => sd} = attrs) when sd not in [nil, ""],
    do: Map.delete(attrs, "date")

  defp rename_date_key(%{scheduled_date: sd} = attrs) when sd not in [nil, ""],
    do: Map.delete(attrs, :date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{"date" => date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete("date") |> Map.put("scheduled_date", date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{date: date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete(:date) |> Map.put(:scheduled_date, date)

  defp rename_date_key(attrs), do: attrs

  defp validate_time_order(changeset) do
    start_time = get_field(changeset, :start_time)
    end_time = get_field(changeset, :end_time)

    if start_time && end_time && Time.compare(start_time, end_time) != :lt do
      add_error(changeset, :end_time, "must be after the start time")
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  # `agreed_price` arrives as dollars (a `Decimal`, matching the
  # money-handling ADR's rate math); it is rounded half-up and stored
  # as `agreed_price_cents` — the only column ever persisted.
  defp put_agreed_price_cents(changeset) do
    case get_change(changeset, :agreed_price) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      %Decimal{} = amount ->
        cents = amount |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer()
        put_change(changeset, :agreed_price_cents, cents)
    end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan do
  @moduledoc """
  A weekly/biweekly/monthly cadence for a property that materializes a
  series of `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job` rows (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence`).

  `cleaner_id` is the client's *preferred* cleaner (story 846): every
  job generated from this plan defaults to this cleaner, and
  reassigning a single visit away from them is a warning, not a block.
  It is optional — a plan with no preferred cleaner generates
  unassigned jobs and never warns on reassignment.

  `start_time`/`end_time` default to a plain 9am-11am visit window;
  nothing in the plan form asks for these explicitly today, but every
  generated job needs a concrete time to run conflict detection
  against.

  `agreed_price_cents` is optional — a plan with no price generates
  visits with no price either (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence.job_attrs/1`), and completing one of
  those visits skips invoice generation rather than crashing (see
  `CleanerCrm.Billing.generate_for_job/2`).
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          recurrence: :weekly | :biweekly | :monthly | nil,
          start_date: Date.t() | nil,
          occurrence_count: integer() | nil,
          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          agreed_price_cents: integer() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "recurring_plans" do
    field :recurrence, Ecto.Enum, values: [:weekly, :biweekly, :monthly]
    field :start_date, :date
    field :occurrence_count, :integer
    field :start_time, :time, default: ~T[09:00:00]
    field :end_time, :time, default: ~T[11:00:00]
    field :agreed_price_cents, :integer
    field :agreed_price, :decimal, virtual: true

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(property_id cleaner_id recurrence start_date occurrence_count start_time end_time
             agreed_price_cents agreed_price)a

  @doc """
  Changeset for the fully-specified plan a save requires.
  """
  def changeset(plan, attrs) do
    plan
    |> cast(attrs, @fields)
    |> validate_required([:property_id, :recurrence, :start_date, :occurrence_count])
    |> validate_number(:occurrence_count, greater_than: 0)
    |> put_agreed_price_cents()
  end

  @doc """
  Changeset for the live preview as the owner fills in the form —
  every field is optional so the conflict list can update incrementally
  as soon as enough of them are present, well before the plan is valid
  enough to save.
  """
  def preview_changeset(plan, attrs) do
    plan
    |> cast(attrs, @fields)
    |> put_agreed_price_cents()
  end

  # `agreed_price` arrives as dollars (a `Decimal`, matching the
  # money-handling ADR); rounded half-up and stored as
  # `agreed_price_cents` — the only column ever persisted. Mirrors
  # `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job.put_agreed_price_cents/1`.
  defp put_agreed_price_cents(changeset) do
    case get_change(changeset, :agreed_price) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      %Decimal{} = amount ->
        cents = amount |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer()
        put_change(changeset, :agreed_price_cents, cents)
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.ConflictDetector do
  @moduledoc """
  Detects scheduling conflicts against a cleaner's availability blocks
  and already-booked jobs — for a single proposed assignment, or across
  every occurrence in a recurring series (unsaved, or already
  materialized).

  Two distinct reasons, surfaced separately so the UI can say something
  useful:

    * `:unavailable` — the cleaner has a time-off block covering the slot
    * `:overlap` — the cleaner already has another job booked then

  Availability is checked first: a time-off block is the more specific
  reason when both happen to apply.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{AvailabilityBlock, Job, RecurringPlan}
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  @doc """
  Checks one proposed (cleaner, date, time window) assignment.

  `opts`:

    * `:exclude_job_id` — omit a job (the one being reassigned) from
      the overlap check against itself
    * `:exclude_recurring_plan_id` — omit every job generated by this
      plan — its own sibling occurrences are not a conflict with each
      other

  Returns `:ok` when the cleaner is `nil` — an unassigned job never
  conflicts.
  """
  def check_assignment(scope, cleaner_id, date, start_time, end_time, opts \\ [])

  def check_assignment(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
        cleaner_id,
        %Date{} = date,
        start_time,
        end_time,
        opts
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) and not is_nil(cleaner_id) do
    cond do
      unavailable?(account_id, cleaner_id, date, start_time, end_time) ->
        {:error, :unavailable}

      overlaps_existing_job?(account_id, cleaner_id, date, start_time, end_time, opts) ->
        {:error, :overlap}

      true ->
        :ok
    end
  end

  def check_assignment(_scope, nil, _date, _start_time, _end_time, _opts), do: :ok

  @doc """
  Checks every occurrence of a plan's series (`[%{index:, date:}, ...]`,
  as returned by `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence.occurrences/1`)
  against that plan's preferred cleaner. Works the same whether the
  plan is unsaved (a live preview) or already saved with its jobs
  materialized — in the latter case, the plan's own jobs are excluded
  from the overlap check against themselves. Returns only the
  conflicting occurrences, as `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
  """
  def check_occurrences(_scope, %RecurringPlan{cleaner_id: nil}, _occurrences), do: []

  def check_occurrences(scope, %RecurringPlan{} = plan, occurrences) do
    opts = [exclude_recurring_plan_id: plan.id]

    occurrences
    |> Enum.map(fn %{index: index, date: date} ->
      case check_assignment(scope, plan.cleaner_id, date, plan.start_time, plan.end_time, opts) do
        :ok -> nil
        {:error, reason} -> %{index: index, date: date, reason: reason}
      end
    end)
    |> Enum.reject(&is_nil/1)
  end

  defp unavailable?(account_id, cleaner_id, date, start_time, end_time) do
    AvailabilityBlock
    |> where(
      [b],
      b.account_id == ^account_id and b.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and b.date == ^date
    )
    |> Repo.all()
    |> Enum.any?(&blocks?(&1, start_time, end_time))
  end

  defp blocks?(%AvailabilityBlock{all_day: true}, _start_time, _end_time), do: true

  defp blocks?(
         %AvailabilityBlock{start_time: block_start, end_time: block_end},
         start_time,
         end_time
       ) do
    overlaps?(block_start, block_end, start_time, end_time)
  end

  defp overlaps_existing_job?(account_id, cleaner_id, date, start_time, end_time, opts) do
    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and
        j.scheduled_date == ^date and j.status != :cancelled
    )
    |> exclude_job(opts[:exclude_job_id])
    |> exclude_plan(opts[:exclude_recurring_plan_id])
    |> Repo.all()
    |> Enum.any?(&overlaps?(&1.start_time, &1.end_time, start_time, end_time))
  end

  defp exclude_job(query, nil), do: query
  defp exclude_job(query, job_id), do: where(query, [j], j.id != ^job_id)

  defp exclude_plan(query, nil), do: query

  defp exclude_plan(query, plan_id) do
    where(query, [j], is_nil(j.recurring_plan_id) or j.recurring_plan_id != ^plan_id)
  end

  defp overlaps?(start_a, end_a, start_b, end_b) do
    Time.compare(start_a, end_b) == :lt and Time.compare(start_b, end_a) == :lt
  end
end

          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  schema "availability_blocks" do

    field :all_day, :boolean, default: false
    field :start_time, :time
    field :end_time, :time

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User

  def changeset(block, attrs) do

    |> cast(attrs, [:cleaner_id, :date, :all_day, :start_time, :end_time])
    |> validate_required([:cleaner_id, :date])

      changeset
    else
      validate_required(changeset, [:start_time, :end_time],
        message: "is required for a partial-day block"
      )
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Money do
  @moduledoc """
  Formats integer cents for display, per the money-handling ADR: every
  amount is stored and computed as integer cents, and this is the only
  place a dollar string gets built.
  """

  @doc """
  Formats integer cents as `"$X.XX"`, with thousands separators. `nil`
  is treated as zero.

  ## Examples

      iex> CleanerCrm.Money.format_cents(18_000)
      "$180.00"

      iex> CleanerCrm.Money.format_cents(nil)
      "$0.00"
  """
  @spec format_cents(integer() | nil) :: String.t()
  def format_cents(nil), do: format_cents(0)

  def format_cents(cents) when is_integer(cents) do
    sign = if cents < 0, do: "-", else: ""
    dollars = div(abs(cents), 100)
    remainder = rem(abs(cents), 100)

    "#{sign}$#{group_thousands(dollars)}.#{pad_cents(remainder)}"
  end

  defp pad_cents(remainder), do: remainder |> Integer.to_string() |> String.pad_leading(2, "0")

  defp group_thousands(dollars) do
    dollars
    |> Integer.to_string()
    |> String.reverse()
    |> String.replace(~r/(\d{3})(?=\d)/, "\\1,")
    |> String.reverse()
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Billing.ReceiptNotifier do
  @moduledoc """
  Emails the client a receipt once a card-on-file or payment-link
  charge has been submitted to Stripe — submitted, not confirmed; per
  the payments-stripe ADR the invoice itself only becomes `:paid` on
  the webhook.
  """

  import Swoosh.Email

  alias CleanerCrm.Billing.Invoice
  alias CleanerCrm.Mailer
  alias CleanerCrm.Money

  def deliver_receipt(email, %Invoice{} = invoice) when is_binary(email) do
    message =
      new()
      |> to(email)
      |> from({"CleanerCrm", "contact@example.com"})
      |> subject("Your receipt")
      |> text_body("""
      Thanks! We've charged #{Money.format_cents(invoice.amount_cents)} for your recent cleaning.

      This confirms the charge was submitted — you'll receive nothing further unless it's declined.
      """)

    Mailer.deliver(message)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.StripeWebhookController do
  @moduledoc """
  Public Stripe webhook endpoint (`POST /webhooks/stripe`) — the only
  place an invoice's payment status ever changes from a pending
  charge, per the payments-stripe ADR. Verification (real signature
  check in production, trusted as-is in test) happens inside
  `CleanerCrm.Billing.receive_webhook/1`, so this controller never
  branches on anything but its result.

  ## Dependencies

  - `CleanerCrm.Billing`
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Billing

  def create(conn, _params) do
    case Billing.receive_webhook(conn) do
      {:ok, _result} ->
        json(conn, %{received: true})

      {:error, _reason} ->
        conn
        |> put_status(:bad_request)
        |> json(%{error: "invalid_signature"})
    end
  end
end

=== Account schema ===
defmodule CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account do
  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          name: String.t(),
          slug: String.t() | nil,
          drive_time_policy: :unpaid | :paid,
          members: [CleanerCrm.Accounts.Member.t()] | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          users: [CleanerCrm.Users.User.t()] | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @reserved_slugs ~w(admin api www help support docs blog)

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "accounts" do
    field :name, :string
    field :slug, :string

    # Whether time spent driving between jobs counts toward a
    # cleaner's pay — read by `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking` alongside a
    # cleaner's earnings, set here rather than on a separate settings
    # table since it's the account's only pay policy so far.
    field :drive_time_policy, Ecto.Enum, values: [:unpaid, :paid], default: :unpaid

    has_many :members, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Member, on_delete: :delete_all
    has_many :users, through: [:members, :user]

    timestamps()
  end

  def changeset(account, attrs) do
    account
    |> cast(attrs, [:name, :slug, :drive_time_policy])
    |> validate_required([:name])
    |> validate_length(:name, min: 1, max: 100)
    |> validate_slug()
    |> unique_constraint(:slug)
  end

  def create_changeset(attrs) do
    %__MODULE__{}
    |> changeset(attrs)
    |> maybe_generate_slug()
  end

  defp validate_slug(changeset) do
    changeset
    |> validate_format(:slug, ~r/^[a-z0-9-]+$/,
      message: "must contain only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens"
    )
    |> validate_length(:slug, min: 3, max: 50)
    |> validate_exclusion(:slug, @reserved_slugs, message: "is reserved and cannot be used")
    |> validate_format(:slug, ~r/^[a-z]/, message: "must start with a letter")
  end

  defp maybe_generate_slug(changeset) do
    case get_field(changeset, :slug) do
      nil ->
        name = get_field(changeset, :name)
        if name, do: put_change(changeset, :slug, generate_slug(name)), else: changeset

      _ ->
        changeset
    end
  end

  defp generate_slug(name) do
    name
    |> String.downcase()
    |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]/, "-")
    |> String.replace(~r/-+/, "-")
    |> String.trim("-")
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Accounts do
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.{Account, AccountsRepository, MembersRepository}
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.{InvitationRepository, InvitationNotifier}
  alias CleanerCrm.Authorization
  alias CleanerCrm.Users
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  def subscribe_account(%Scope{} = scope) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:account")
  end

  def subscribe_member(%Scope{} = scope) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:member")
  end

  defp broadcast_account(%Scope{} = scope, message) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:account", message)
  end

  defp broadcast_member(%Scope{} = scope, message) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:member", message)
  end

  def list_accounts(%Scope{} = scope) do
    MembersRepository.list_user_accounts(scope.user.id)
  end

  def get_account(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
    case AccountsRepository.get_account(id) do
      nil ->
        nil

      account ->
        case Authorization.authorize(:read_account, scope, account.id) do
          false -> nil
          true -> account
        end
    end
  end

  def get_account!(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
    account = AccountsRepository.get_account!(id)
    Authorization.authorize!(:read_account, scope, account.id)
    account
  end

  def create_account(%Scope{} = scope, attrs) do
    with {:ok, account} <- AccountsRepository.create_account_with_owner(attrs, scope.user.id) do
      broadcast_account(scope, {:created, account})
      {:ok, account}
    end
  end

  def update_account(%Scope{} = scope, %Account{} = account, attrs) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account.id)

    with {:ok, account} <- AccountsRepository.update_account(account, attrs) do
      broadcast_account(scope, {:updated, account})
      {:ok, account}
    end
  end

  def delete_account(%Scope{} = scope, %Account{} = account) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account.id)

    with {:ok, account} <- AccountsRepository.delete_account(account) do
      broadcast_account(scope, {:deleted, account})
      {:ok, account}
    end
  end

  def change_account(%Scope{} = scope, %Account{} = account, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account.id)
    Account.changeset(account, attrs)
  end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.QuoteLive.Builder do @moduledoc """ Builds and sends a quote, with live totals as the owner fills it in. The rate card and quote forms live on the same page: a quote is priced by exactly one model at a time, so switching models drops whatever the previous model's inputs held (see `CleanerCrm.Quoting.Pricing.fields_for_model/1`). A quote is only ever persisted at the moment it's sent — before that, everything here is in-memory socket state. ## Routes * `/quotes/new` (`:new`) — build and send a new quote. * `/quotes/:id` (`:show`) — a previously sent quote, frozen against later rate-card changes. ## Dependencies - `CleanerCrm.Quoting` """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view alias CleanerCrm.Money alias CleanerCrm.Quoting alias CleanerCrm.Quoting.{Pricing, Quote} @impl true def render(%{live_action: :show} = assigns) do ~H""" <.header> {@quote.client_name || "Unnamed lead"} <:subtitle>{pricing_model_label(@quote.pricing_model)} quote <:actions> <.button navigate={~p"/quotes"} class="btn-sm btn-ghost">Back to Quotes

Status: {status_label(@quote.status)}

Phone: {@quote.client_phone}

  • {item.description} × {item.quantity} @ {Money.format_cents(item.rate_cents)}
    {Money.format_cents(item.amount_cents)}

Total: {Money.format_cents(@quote.total_cents)}

""" end def render(assigns) do ~H""" <.header> New Quote <:subtitle>Price a job by room, square footage, or hours

Rate Card

<.form for={@rate_card_form} id="rate-card-form" data-test="rate-card-form" phx-submit="save_rate_card" > <.input field={@rate_card_form[:per_room_bedroom_rate_cents]} type="number" label="Per-bedroom rate (cents)" /> <.input field={@rate_card_form[:per_room_bathroom_rate_cents]} type="number" label="Per-bathroom rate (cents)" /> <.input field={@rate_card_form[:per_sqft_rate_cents]} type="number" label="Per-square-foot rate (cents)" /> <.input field={@rate_card_form[:hourly_rate_cents]} type="number" label="Hourly rate (cents)" />
<.button phx-disable-with="Saving...">Save Rate Card

Quote Details

<.form for={@form} id="quote-form" data-test="quote-form" phx-change="validate" phx-submit="validate" > <.input field={@form[:client_name]} type="text" label="Client name" /> <.input field={@form[:client_phone]} type="text" label="Client phone" /> <.input field={@form[:pricing_model]} type="select" label="Pricing model" prompt="Select a pricing model" options={[ {"Per room", :per_room}, {"Per square foot", :per_sqft}, {"Hourly", :hourly} ]} /> <%!-- Every model's inputs stay mounted at all times (never added or removed from the DOM) so a single form change can set a pricing model and its own field together in one round trip. Only the visible model's group loses the `hidden` class, and only its inputs carry a `data-test` attribute — the other models' fields are inert without either. --%>
<.input field={@form[:bedroom_count]} type="number" label="Bedrooms" data-test={active_field(@pricing_model, :per_room, "room-bedroom-count-input")} /> <.input field={@form[:bathroom_count]} type="number" label="Bathrooms" data-test={active_field(@pricing_model, :per_room, "room-bathroom-count-input")} />
<.input field={@form[:square_feet]} type="number" label="Square feet" data-test={active_field(@pricing_model, :per_sqft, "square-feet-input")} />
<.input field={@form[:hours]} type="number" label="Hours" data-test={active_field(@pricing_model, :hourly, "hours-input")} />

Total: {Money.format_cents(@total_cents)}

Add a rate for this pricing model on your rate card before sending this quote.

<.button type="button" phx-click="send_quote" data-test="send-quote-button" variant="primary" > Send Quote
""" end @impl true def mount(_params, _session, socket), do: {:ok, socket} @impl true def handle_params(params, _url, socket) do {:noreply, apply_action(socket, socket.assigns.live_action, params)} end defp apply_action(socket, :new, _params) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope rate_card = Quoting.get_or_create_rate_card(scope) changeset = Quoting.change_quote(scope, %Quote{}) socket |> assign(:page_title, "New Quote") |> assign(:rate_card, rate_card) |> assign(:rate_card_form, to_form(Quoting.change_rate_card(scope, rate_card))) |> recalculate(changeset) end defp apply_action(socket, :show, %{"id" => id}) do quote = Quoting.get_quote!(socket.assigns.current_scope, id) socket |> assign(:page_title, quote.client_name || "Quote") |> assign(:quote, quote) end @impl true def handle_event("validate", %{"quote" => quote_params}, socket) do changeset = socket.assigns.current_scope |> Quoting.change_quote(%Quote{}, sanitize_quote_params(quote_params)) |> Map.put(:action, :validate) {:noreply, recalculate(socket, changeset)} end def handle_event("save_rate_card", %{"rate_card" => rate_card_params}, socket) do %{current_scope: scope, rate_card: rate_card, form: form} = socket.assigns case Quoting.update_rate_card(scope, rate_card, rate_card_params) do {:ok, rate_card} -> {:noreply, socket |> assign(:rate_card, rate_card) |> assign(:rate_card_form, to_form(Quoting.change_rate_card(scope, rate_card))) |> recalculate(form.source)} {:error, changeset} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :rate_card_form, to_form(changeset))} end end def handle_event("send_quote", _params, socket) do %{current_scope: scope, quote_draft: draft, rate_card: rate_card} = socket.assigns case Quoting.send_quote(scope, draft, rate_card) do {:ok, quote} -> {:noreply, push_patch(socket, to: ~p"/quotes/#{quote}")} {:error, :not_finalizable} -> {:noreply, socket} end end defp recalculate(socket, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset) do quote_draft = Ecto.Changeset.apply_changes(changeset) line_items = Pricing.line_items(socket.assigns.rate_card, quote_draft) socket |> assign(:form, to_form(changeset)) |> assign(:quote_draft, quote_draft) |> assign(:pricing_model, quote_draft.pricing_model) |> assign(:total_cents, Pricing.total_cents(line_items)) |> assign(:missing_rate?, Pricing.missing_rate?(line_items)) end # The `data-test` attribute for a model-specific input: present only # while its model is the one currently selected, `nil` (i.e. omitted # entirely) otherwise — the input itself always stays in the DOM. defp defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

  import Plug.Conn
  import Phoenix.Controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Users
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  # Make the remember me cookie valid for 14 days. This should match
  # the session validity setting in UserToken.
  @max_cookie_age_in_days 14
  @remember_me_cookie "_cleaner_crm_web_user_remember_me"
  @remember_me_options [
    sign: true,
    max_age: @max_cookie_age_in_days * 24 * 60 * 60,
    same_site: "Lax"
  ]

  # How old the session token should be before a new one is issued. When a request is made
  # with a session token older than this value, then a new session token will be created
  # and the session and remember-me cookies (if set) will be updated with the new token.
  # Lowering this value will result in more tokens being created by active users. Increasing
  # it will result in less time before a session token expires for a user to get issued a new
  # token. This can be set to a value greater than `@max_cookie_age_in_days` to disable
  # the reissuing of tokens completely.
  @session_reissue_age_in_days 7

  @doc """
  Logs the user in.

  Redirects to the session's `:user_return_to` path
  or falls back to the `signed_in_path/1`.
  """
  def log_in_user(conn, user, params \\ %{}) do
    user_return_to = get_session(conn, :user_return_to)

    conn
    |> create_or_extend_session(user, params)
    |> redirect(to: user_return_to || signed_in_path(conn))
  end

  @doc """
  Logs the user out.

  It clears all session data for safety. See renew_session.
  """
  def log_out_user(conn) do
    user_token = get_session(conn, :user_token)
    user_token && Users.delete_user_session_token(user_token)

    if live_socket_id = get_session(conn, :live_socket_id) do
      CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.broadcast(live_socket_id, "disconnect", %{})
    end

    conn
    |> renew_session(nil)
    |> delete_resp_cookie(@remember_me_cookie, @remember_me_options)
    |> redirect(to: ~p"/")
  end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Clients.Client do
  @moduledoc """
  A paying customer with contact info and preferences.

  Scoped to an account: every client belongs to exactly one account and
  is only ever visible within that account.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          name: String.t() | nil,
          active: boolean(),
          card_on_file: boolean(),
          email: String.t() | nil,
          phone: String.t() | nil,
          preferred_channel: :email | :sms,
          properties: [CleanerCrm.Clients.Property.t()] | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "clients" do
    field :name, :string
    field :active, :boolean, default: true
    field :card_on_file, :boolean, default: false
    field :email, :string
    field :phone, :string
    field :preferred_channel, Ecto.Enum, values: [:email, :sms], default: :email

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    has_many :properties, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  def changeset(client, attrs) do
    client
    |> cast(attrs, [:name, :active, :card_on_file, :email, :phone, :preferred_channel])
    |> validate_required([:name], message: "is required")
    |> validate_length(:name, min: 1, max: 200)
  end
end

  defp blank_client_id_to_nil(attrs), do: attrs

defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications do
  @moduledoc """
  Client appointment reminders with confirm/reschedule actions, and
  cleaner schedule-change alerts requiring explicit acknowledgment with
  office visibility into what's still unacknowledged. Email/SMS
  delivery is abstracted behind `CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery`.

  Most functions are scoped by the caller's `Scope`. The confirm,
  reschedule, and delivery-status webhook endpoints are reached by an
  unauthenticated client or provider, so they look a notification up by
  its opaque `token` (or the provider's message id) instead.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications.{
    Notification,
    ReminderNotifier,
    ReminderScheduler,
    ReminderSettings
  }

  ## Reminder settings

  @doc "The account's reminder settings, defaulting to a 24-hour lead time if never configured."
  def get_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(ReminderSettings, account_id: account_id) do
      nil -> %ReminderSettings{account_id: account_id}
      settings -> settings

defmodule CleanerCrm.Mailer do
  use Swoosh.Mailer, otp_app: :cleaner_crm

defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications do
  @moduledoc """
  Client appointment reminders with confirm/reschedule actions, and
  cleaner schedule-change alerts requiring explicit acknowledgment with
  office visibility into what's still unacknowledged. Email/SMS
  delivery is abstracted behind `CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery`.

  Most functions are scoped by the caller's `Scope`. The confirm,
  reschedule, and delivery-status webhook endpoints are reached by an
  unauthenticated client or provider, so they look a notification up by
  its opaque `token` (or the provider's message id) instead.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications.{
    Notification,
    ReminderNotifier,
    ReminderScheduler,
    ReminderSettings
  }

  ## Reminder settings

  @doc "The account's reminder settings, defaulting to a 24-hour lead time if never configured."
  def get_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(ReminderSettings, account_id: account_id) do
      nil -> %ReminderSettings{account_id: account_id}
      settings -> settings
    end
  end

  def change_reminder_settings(%Scope{} = scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope |> get_reminder_settings() |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
  end

  def update_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> get_reminder_settings()
    |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert_or_update()
  end

  @doc "Runs the periodic reminder scan now — see `CleanerCrm.Notifications.ReminderScheduler`."
  defdelegate send_due_reminders(), to: ReminderScheduler, as: :scan_and_send

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence do
  @moduledoc """
  Generates the dates for a plan's series from its cadence.

  Project-local, calendar-date arithmetic (see the recurrence ADR) —
  no RRULE library, no virtual occurrences. `:weekly` steps 7 days,
  `:biweekly` 14, `:monthly` 28 (a fixed 4-week cadence, not a calendar
  month, so the weekday never drifts).

  TODO: the recurrence ADR calls for materializing against each
  account's IANA timezone (via `tzdata`) so visits stay pinned to local
  wall-clock across DST, plus a rolling 12-week horizon extended by a
  daily Oban job. Neither is implemented yet — dates here are naive
  and every plan is materialized in full up front, bounded only by its
  own `occurrence_count`.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan

  @step_days %{weekly: 7, biweekly: 14, monthly: 28}

  @doc """
  Returns a list of `%{index:, date:}` maps, one per occurrence, in
  series order starting at 1. `nil` if the plan is missing any of the
  fields a series needs.
  """
  def occurrences(%RecurringPlan{
        recurrence: recurrence,
        start_date: %Date{} = start_date,
        occurrence_count: count
      })
      when recurrence in [:weekly, :biweekly, :monthly] and is_integer(count) and count > 0 do
    step = Map.fetch!(@step_days, recurrence)

    for index <- 1..count do
      %{index: index, date: Date.add(start_date, (index - 1) * step)}
    end
  end

  def occurrences(_incomplete_plan), do: []

  @doc """
  Job attribute maps ready for `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.create_job/2`, one
  per occurrence. Carries the plan's `agreed_price_cents` (`nil` when
  the plan has none) onto every occurrence — `CleanerCrm.Billing`
  handles a `nil` price on job completion gracefully rather than
  crashing, but a priced plan should still price its own visits.
  """
  def job_attrs(%RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
    Enum.map(occurrences(plan), fn %{date: date} ->
      %{
        property_id: plan.property_id,
        cleaner_id: plan.cleaner_id,
        recurring_plan_id: plan.id,
        scheduled_date: date,
        start_time: plan.start_time,
        end_time: plan.end_time,
        agreed_price_cents: plan.agreed_price_cents
      }
    end)
  end
end

        new_state
        |> push_pending_events_on_redirect(new_socket)
        |> push_live_redirect(opts, ref)
        |> then(fn state ->
          if new_socket.sticky? do
            {:noreply, drop_redirect(state)}
          else
            stop_shutdown_redirect(state, :live_redirect, opts)
          end
        end)

      {:live, :patch, %{to: _to, kind: _kind} = opts} when root_pid == self() ->
        {params, action} = patch_params_and_action!(new_socket, opts)

        new_state
        |> drop_redirect()
        |> check_patch_redirect_limit!()
        |> Map.update!(:socket, &Utils.replace_flash(&1, flash))
        |> sync_handle_params_with_live_redirect(params, action, opts, ref)

      {:live, :patch, %{to: _to, kind: _kind}} = patch ->
        send(new_socket.root_pid, {@prefix, :redirect, patch, flash})
        {:diff, diff, new_state} = render_diff(new_state, new_socket, false)

        {:noreply,
         new_state
         |> drop_redirect()
         |> push_diff(diff, ref)}
    end
  end

  defp push_pending_events_on_redirect(state, socket) do
    if diff = Diff.get_push_events_diff(socket), do: push_diff(state, diff, nil)
    state
  end

  defp patch_params_and_action!(socket, %{to: to}) do
    destructure [path, query], :binary.split(to, ["?", "#"], [:global])
    to = %{socket.host_uri | path: path, query: query}

    case Route.live_link_info!(socket, socket.private.root_view, to) do
      {:internal, %Route{params: params, action: action}} ->
        {params, action}

      {:external, _uri} ->
        raise ArgumentError,
              "cannot push_patch/2 to #{inspect(to)} because the given path " <>
                "does not point to the current root view #{inspect(socket.private.root_view)}"
    end
  end

  defp stop_shutdown_redirect(state, kind, opts) do
    send(state.socket.transport_pid, {:socket_close, self(), {kind, opts}})
    {:stop, {:shutdown, {kind, opts}}, state}
  end

  defp drop_redirect(state) do
    put_in(state.socket.redirected, nil)
  end

  defp sync_handle_params_with_live_redirect(state, params, action, %{to: to} = opts, ref) do
    %{socket: socket} = state

    {:noreply, %Socket{} = new_socket} =
      socket
      |> assign_action(action)
      |> Utils.call_handle_params!(socket.view, params, build_uri(state, to))

    handle_changed(state, new_socket, ref, opts)

## Examples

      render_click(view, :event_that_triggers_page_title_update)
      assert page_title(view) =~ "my title"

  """
  def page_title(view) do
    call(view, :page_title)
  end

  @doc """
  Asserts a live patch will happen within `timeout` milliseconds.
  The default `timeout` is [ExUnit](https://ex-unit.hexdocs.pm/ExUnit.html#configure/1)'s
  `assert_receive_timeout` (100 ms).

  It returns the new path.

  To assert on the flash message, you can assert on the result of the
  rendered LiveView.

  ## Examples

      render_click(view, :event_that_triggers_patch)
      assert_patch view

      render_click(view, :event_that_triggers_patch)
      assert_patch view, 30

      render_click(view, :event_that_triggers_patch)
      path = assert_patch view
      assert path =~ ~r/path/\d+/

defmodule CleanerCrm.Users.Scope do
  @moduledoc """
  Defines the scope of the caller to be used throughout the app.

  The `CleanerCrm.Users.Scope` allows public interfaces to receive
  information about the caller, such as if the call is initiated from an
  end-user, and if so, which user. Additionally, such a scope can carry fields
  such as "super user" or other privileges for use in authorization checks,
  or to ensure specific code paths can only be accessed for a given scope.

  It is useful for logging as well as for scoping pubsub subscriptions and
  broadcasts when a caller subscribes to an interface or performs a particular
  action.

  Feel free to extend the fields on this struct to fit the needs of
  growing application requirements.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  defstruct user: nil,
            active_account: nil,
            active_account_id: nil

  @doc """
  Creates a scope for the given user.

  Returns nil if no user is given.
  """
  def for_user(%User{} = user) do
    %__MODULE__{user: user}
  end

  def for_user(nil), do: nil
end
---

defmodule CleanerCrm.Accounts.AccountsRepository do
  import Ecto.Query, warn: false
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.{Account, Member}

  def create_account(attrs) do
    %Account{}
    |> Account.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  def get_account(id), do: Repo.get(Account, id)
  def get_account!(id), do: Repo.get!(Account, id)

  def update_account(%Account{} = account, attrs) do
    account
    |> Account.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  def delete_account(%Account{} = account), do: Repo.delete(account)

  def create_account_with_owner(attrs, owner_id) do
    Repo.transaction(fn ->
      with {:ok, account} <- create_account(attrs),
           {:ok, _member} <-
             create_member(%{user_id: owner_id, account_id: account.id, role: :owner}) do
        account
      else
        {:error, reason} -> Repo.rollback(reason)
      end
    end)
  end

  def by_slug(slug), do: from(a in Account, where: a.slug == ^slug)
  def with_preloads(preloads), do: preload(Account, ^preloads)

  defp create_member(attrs) do
    %Member{}
    |> Member.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb do
  @moduledoc """
  The entrypoint for defining your web interface, such
  as controllers, components, channels, and so on.

  This can be used in your application as:

      use CleanerCrmWeb, :controller
      use CleanerCrmWeb, :html

  The definitions below will be executed for every controller,
  component, etc, so keep them short and clean, focused
  on imports, uses and aliases.

  Do NOT define functions inside the quoted expressions
  below. Instead, define additional modules and import
  those modules here.
  """

  use Boundary, deps: [CleanerCrm], exports: :all

  def static_paths, do: ~w(assets fonts images favicon.ico robots.txt)

  def router do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Router, helpers: false

      # Import common connection and controller functions to use in pipelines
      import Plug.Conn
      import Phoenix.Controller
      import Phoenix.LiveView.Router
    end
  end

  def channel do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Channel
    end
  end

  def controller do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Controller, formats: [:html, :json]

      use Gettext, backend: CleanerCrmWeb.Gettext

      import Plug.Conn

      unquote(verified_routes())
    end
  end

  def live_view do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.LiveView

      unquote(html_helpers())
    end
  end

  def live_component do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.LiveComponent

      unquote(html_helpers())
    end
  end

  def html do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Component

      # Import convenience functions from controllers
      import Phoenix.Controller,
        only: [get_csrf_token: 0, view_module: 1, view_template: 1]

      # Include general helpers for rendering HTML
      unquote(html_helpers())
    end
  end

  defp html_helpers do
    quote do
      # Translation
      use Gettext, backend: CleanerCrmWeb.Gettext

      # HTML escaping functionality
      import Phoenix.HTML
      # Core UI components
      import CleanerCrmWeb.CoreComponents

      # Common modules used in templates
      alias Phoenix.LiveView.JS
      alias CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts

      # Routes generation with the ~p sigil
      unquote(verified_routes())
    end
  end

  def verified_routes do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.VerifiedRoutes,
        endpoint: CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
        router: CleanerCrmWeb.Router,
        statics: CleanerCrmWeb.static_paths()
    end
  end

  @doc """
  When used, dispatch to the appropriate controller/live_view/etc.
  """
  defmacro __using__(which) when is_atom(which) do
    apply(__MODULE__, which, [])
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling do
  @moduledoc """
  Recurring plans and the jobs they generate, cleaner time-off, and
  conflict-aware assignment.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Property
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{
    AvailabilityBlock,
    ConflictDetector,
    Job,
    Recurrence,
    RecurringPlan
  }

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  ## Jobs

  def get_job!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_job(%Scope{}, %Job{} = job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Job.changeset(job, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a job. Recorded in the audit trail as authored by the
  caller, unless `actor: :system` is passed — used when the job is one
  occurrence materialized from a recurring plan rather than a job a
  human directly asked for (see `create_recurring_plan/2`).
  """
  def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs, opts \\ [])
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, job} <-
           %Job{account_id: account_id}
           |> Job.changeset(derive_client_id(account_id, attrs))
           |> Repo.insert() do
      record_job_created(scope, job, Keyword.get(opts, :actor, :user))
      {:ok, job}
    end
  end

  # The board's own job form (and a recurring plan's own materialized
  # occurrences, via `Recurrence.job_attrs/1`) only ever carry a
  # `property_id` — never a `client_id` — so a job created either way
  # otherwise saves with `client_id: nil`. That breaks anything reading
  # the client straight off the job rather than through its property
  # (story 836's invoicing does both a card-on-file charge lookup and
  # the invoice's own client label this way), so every job creation
  # backfills `client_id` from its property here rather than requiring
  # every caller to remember to. A caller that already supplies a
  # `client_id` (fixtures with only a client on hand, no property) is
  # left alone.
  defp derive_client_id(account_id, attrs) do
    if blank?(fetch_attr(attrs, :client_id)) do
      case fetch_attr(attrs, :property_id) do
        value when value in [nil, ""] -> attrs
        property_id -> put_client_id_from_property(attrs, account_id, property_id)
      end
    else
      attrs
    end
  end

  defp put_client_id_from_property(attrs, account_id, property_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Property, id: property_id, account_id: account_id) do
      %Property{client_id: client_id} when not is_nil(client_id) ->
        # Match whichever key style (atom or string) `attrs` already
        # uses — `Ecto.Changeset.cast/4` raises on a map mixing both.
        if Map.has_key?(attrs, :property_id) do
          Map.put(attrs, :client_id, client_id)
        else
          Map.put(attrs, "client_id", client_id)
        end

      _ ->
        attrs
    end
  end

  defp fetch_attr(attrs, key), do: Map.get(attrs, key) || Map.get(attrs, to_string(key))

  defp blank?(nil), do: true
  defp blank?(""), do: true
  defp blank?(_value), do: false

  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :system) do
    Recorder.record_system(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
  end

  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :user) do
    Recorder.record(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
  end

  # Deliberately omits `scheduled_date`: a "created" entry's own
  # subject label (job → property/client) is enough to identify which
  # job this is, and surfacing it here would read as a schedule change
  # (`field_changes/1`'s "Scheduled date: ..." line) indistinguishable
  # from an actual reschedule recorded later by `update_job/3`.
  defp job_created_values(job) do
    %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id}
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every job scheduled between `week_start` and six days later,
  cleaner/property/client preloaded, ordered for the board.
  """
  def list_jobs_for_week(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Date{} = week_start)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    week_end = Date.add(week_start, 6)

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date >= ^week_start and
        j.scheduled_date <= ^week_end and j.status != :cancelled
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every non-cancelled job for the account, cleaner/property/client
  preloaded, ordered for the board. Unlike `list_jobs_for_week/2`, this
  isn't bounded to a single week — a recurring plan's series can span
  months, and the board needs to account for all of it at a glance.

  `:include_cancelled_ids` (default `[]`) admits specific cancelled
  jobs back in anyway — the board's own escape hatch for a cancelled
  job that still carries an unacknowledged schedule-change
  notification (story 843): the office needs to keep seeing its
  ack-status until the cleaner acknowledges, and the escalation check
  needs the job rendered at all to ever run. Other callers passing no
  opts see the same non-cancelled set as before.
  """
  def list_jobs(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, opts \\ [])
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    include_cancelled_ids = Keyword.get(opts, :include_cancelled_ids, [])

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and
        (j.status != :cancelled or j.id in ^include_cancelled_ids)
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Assigns (or reassigns) a job to a cleaner, rejecting the move with
  `{:error, :unavailable}` or `{:error, :overlap}` when it conflicts
  with that cleaner's time off or an existing booking. A `nil`
  `cleaner_id` always succeeds (unassigning never conflicts).
  """
  def assign_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <-
           ConflictDetector.check_assignment(
             scope,
             cleaner_id,
             job.scheduled_date,
             job.start_time,
             job.end_time,
             exclude_job_id: job.id
           ),
         {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_reassigned",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id},
        %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def cancel_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_cancelled",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Updates a job's schedule and/or price — a reschedule, a price
  change, or both, made directly from the board rather than through
  `assign_cleaner/3`'s conflict-checked path. Records only the fields
  that actually changed to the audit trail, attributed to the caller.
  """
  def update_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    changeset = Job.changeset(job, derive_client_id(account_id, attrs))

    with {:ok, updated} <- Repo.update(changeset) do
      record_job_updated(scope, job, changeset, updated)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  @audited_update_fields ~w(scheduled_date start_time end_time agreed_price_cents status)a

  defp record_job_updated(scope, job, changeset, updated) do
    changed_fields =
      changeset.changes
      |> Map.keys()
      |> Enum.filter(&(&1 in @audited_update_fields))

    if changed_fields != [] do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        update_action(changed_fields),
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        audit_snapshot(job, changed_fields),
        audit_snapshot(updated, changed_fields)
      )
    end
  end

  defp update_action(changed_fields) do
    cond do
      Enum.any?(changed_fields, &(&1 in [:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])) ->
        "job_rescheduled"

      :agreed_price_cents in changed_fields ->
        "job_price_changed"

      true ->
        "job_updated"
    end
  end

  defp audit_snapshot(job, fields),
    do: Map.new(fields, &{to_string(&1), audit_value(Map.get(job, &1))})

  defp audit_value(%Date{} = value), do: to_string(value)
  defp audit_value(%Time{} = value), do: to_string(value)
  defp audit_value(value), do: value

  @doc """
  Removes a job from the board without hard-deleting its row — the
  row (and any audit entries already about it) stays resolvable for
  the trail. Distinct from `cancel_job/2`: this is the office
  correcting a mistaken entry rather than calling off an appointment,
  so it's recorded as "deleted" rather than "cancelled" and never
  notifies the assigned cleaner.
  """
  def delete_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_deleted",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  ## Recurring plans

  def get_recurring_plan!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    RecurringPlan
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:property, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_recurring_plan(%Scope{}, %RecurringPlan{} = plan, attrs \\ %{}) do
    RecurringPlan.preview_changeset(plan, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Runs conflict detection for a (possibly unsaved) plan's full series
  against its preferred cleaner, without persisting anything. Returns
  only the conflicting occurrences, as `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
  """
  def preview_conflicts(scope, %RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
    ConflictDetector.check_occurrences(scope, plan, Recurrence.occurrences(plan))
  end

  @doc """
  Saves a recurring plan and materializes its full series of jobs.
  Conflicting occurrences are still created and still assigned to the
  preferred cleaner — conflicts are for the owner to review and
  resolve, never a silent block on saving.
  """
  def create_recurring_plan(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, plan} <-
             %RecurringPlan{account_id: account_id}
             |> RecurringPlan.changeset(attrs)
             |> Repo.insert() do
        jobs =
          plan
          |> Recurrence.job_attrs()
          |> Enum.map(fn job_attrs ->
            {:ok, job} = create_job(scope, job_attrs, actor: :system)
            job
          end)

        {:ok, {plan, jobs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  ## Availability blocks

  def change_availability_block(%Scope{}, %AvailabilityBlock{} = block, attrs \\ %{}) do
    AvailabilityBlock.changeset(block, attrs)
  end

  def create_availability_block(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %AvailabilityBlock{account_id: account_id}
    |> AvailabilityBlock.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Cleaners (account members who take jobs)

  @doc """
  Lists the account's members as candidate cleaners for the board and
  assignment pickers.
  """
  def list_cleaners(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> Accounts.list_account_members(account_id)
    |> Enum.map(& &1.user)
  end

  @doc """
  Registers a new cleaner: a user identified by display name (rather
  than login credentials) added to the account as a member, so jobs
  and availability can be assigned to them. There is no login flow for
  a cleaner created this way — see `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3`
  for the (real, login-capable) path other stories seed cleaners
  through.
  """
  def register_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, name)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(name) do
    with {:ok, user} <- insert_cleaner_user(name),
         {:ok, _member} <- Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account_id, :member) do
      {:ok, user}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Fetches a single cleaner by id, for their detail page. Draws from
  the same membership list as `list_cleaners/1`, so a user who isn't
  a member of this account can't be looked up here either. Raises if
  not found.
  """
  def get_cleaner!(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
    cleaner_id = parse_cleaner_id(id)

    scope
    |> list_cleaners()
    |> Enum.find(&(&1.id == cleaner_id))
    |> case do
      nil -> raise Ecto.NoResultsError, queryable: User
      cleaner -> cleaner
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Lists a cleaner's time-off blocks for their detail page, soonest
  first.
  """
  def list_availability_blocks(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    cleaner_id = parse_cleaner_id(cleaner_id)

    AvailabilityBlock
    |> where([b], b.account_id == ^account_id and b.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id)
    |> order_by([b], asc: b.date)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists a cleaner's upcoming (today or later, non-cancelled) jobs for
  their detail page, soonest first.
  """
  def list_upcoming_jobs_for_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    cleaner_id = parse_cleaner_id(cleaner_id)

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and
        j.status != :cancelled and j.scheduled_date >= ^Date.utc_today()
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  defp parse_cleaner_id(id) when is_integer(id), do: id
  defp parse_cleaner_id(id) when is_binary(id), do: String.to_integer(id)

  defp insert_cleaner_user(name) do
    %User{}
    |> Ecto.Changeset.cast(%{name: name, email: placeholder_email(name)}, [:name, :email])
    |> Ecto.Changeset.validate_required([:name, :email])
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp placeholder_email(name) do
    slug =
      name
      |> String.downcase()
      |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]+/, ".")
      |> String.trim(".")

    "#{slug}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@cleaners.local"
  end

  ## Cancellation policy (story 851)

  @doc """
  Sets the account's reschedule/cancel policy. A thin delegate onto
  `CleanerCrm.Portal`, which actually owns `CancellationPolicy` (the
  client portal's own reschedule/cancel enforcement is what reads it
  back) — kept reachable here too since "the account's scheduling
  policy" is naturally where a caller that doesn't otherwise need to
  know about the portal would look for it.
  """
  defdelegate set_cancellation_policy(scope, attrs), to: CleanerCrm.Portal
end

A single row per account (see `CleanerCrm.Quoting.get_or_create_rate_card/1`).
  A rate left blank means that pricing model isn't priced yet — quoting
  against it is refused until the owner sets a rate (see
  `CleanerCrm.Quoting.Pricing`).

  `weekly_discount_percent`/`biweekly_discount_percent`/`monthly_discount_percent`
  and `add_on_rates_cents` exist for the public instant-quote calculator
  (story 848, see `CleanerCrm.Booking.Pricing`) — a recurring frequency's
  discount off the one-time subtotal, and the configured price for each
  named add-on (e.g. `"inside_fridge" => 1500`). Unset (`nil`) means no
  discount; an add-on key missing from the map means it isn't priced
  yet, same "never guess a price" rule as the base rates.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          per_room_bedroom_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          per_room_bathroom_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          per_sqft_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          hourly_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          weekly_discount_percent: integer() | nil,
          biweekly_discount_percent: integer() | nil,
          monthly_discount_percent: integer() | nil,
          add_on_rates_cents: %{optional(String.t()) => integer()},
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "rate_cards" do
    field :per_room_bedroom_rate_cents, :integer
    field :per_room_bathroom_rate_cents, :integer
    field :per_sqft_rate_cents, :integer
    field :hourly_rate_cents, :integer
    field :weekly_discount_percent, :integer
    field :biweekly_discount_percent, :integer
    field :monthly_discount_percent, :integer
    field :add_on_rates_cents, :map, default: %{}

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @rate_fields ~w(per_room_bedroom_rate_cents per_room_bathroom_rate_cents
                  per_sqft_rate_cents hourly_rate_cents weekly_discount_percent
                  biweekly_discount_percent monthly_discount_percent add_on_rates_cents)a

  @discount_fields ~w(weekly_discount_percent biweekly_discount_percent monthly_discount_percent)a

  def changeset(rate_card, attrs) do
    rate_card
    |> cast(attrs, @rate_fields)
    |> validate_number(:per_room_bedroom_rate_cents, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> validate_number(:per_room_bathroom_rate_cents, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)

  `CleanerCrm.Quoting.Pricing`).
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          per_room_bedroom_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          per_room_bathroom_rate_cents: integer() | nil,

          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,

    field :per_room_bedroom_rate_cents, :integer
    field :per_room_bathroom_rate_cents, :integer
    field :per_sqft_rate_cents, :integer
    field :hourly_rate_cents, :integer

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @rate_fields ~w(per_room_bedroom_rate_cents per_room_bathroom_rate_cents
                  per_sqft_rate_cents hourly_rate_cents)a

  def changeset(rate_card, attrs) do
    rate_card

@doc """
  Whether the account has no non-cancelled job overlapping this exact
  date/time window, regardless of cleaner assignment.

  This is the coarser, single-crew-capacity check the public booking
  funnel (`CleanerCrm.Booking`) needs before confirming a slot — as
  opposed to `assign_cleaner/3`'s `ConflictDetector`, which is scoped
  to one specific cleaner's own calendar and never conflicts with an
  unassigned job.
  """
  def slot_available?(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Date{} = date, start_time, end_time)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date == ^date and j.status != :cancelled
    )
    |> Repo.all()
    |> Enum.all?(&(not overlaps?(&1.start_time, &1.end_time, start_time, end_time)))
  end

  defp overlaps?(start_a, end_a, start_b, end_b) do
    Time.compare(start_a, end_b) == :lt and Time.compare(start_b, end_a) == :lt
  end

  ## Recurring plans

defmodule CleanerCrm.Booking.Lead do
  @moduledoc """
  A public instant-quote submission (story 848/849): the property
  inputs and frequency/add-ons it was priced from, the price snapshot
  frozen at the moment contact info was captured, the client's contact
  details, and everything the acceptance flow (slot, cancellation-policy
  agreement, card) adds on top of it.

  ## Status

  `:quoted` — never actually persisted today (the calculator on `/book`
  prices a lead purely in memory, see `CleanerCrm.Booking.change_lead/2`)
  but kept as the schema default for a row that, in principle, exists
  before contact info locks it in.

  `:accepted` -> `:payment_pending` -> `:converted`, or `:payment_pending`
  -> `:payment_declined` (from which the client can retry). Only a
  Stripe webhook (`CleanerCrm.Booking.receive_payment_webhook/1`) ever
  moves a lead into `:converted` or `:payment_declined` — submitting
  the card just moves it to `:payment_pending`, per the same
  webhook-confirms-everything rule `CleanerCrm.Billing` follows for
  invoice payments.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type pricing_model :: :per_room | :per_sqft | :hourly
  @type frequency :: :one_time | :weekly | :biweekly | :monthly

defmodule CleanerCrm.Booking.Pricing do
  @moduledoc """
  Prices a `CleanerCrm.Booking.Lead` from the account's rate card:
  the base per-room/per-sqft/hourly amount (reusing
  `CleanerCrm.Quoting.Pricing`, the same math the office quote builder
  uses), each selected add-on's configured amount, and the selected
  frequency's recurring discount off that subtotal.

  Pure and side-effect free, exactly like `CleanerCrm.Quoting.Pricing` —
  `CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.Quote` calls `summarize/2` on every
  keystroke for the live total.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Booking.Lead
  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting.{Quote, RateCard}
  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting.Pricing, as: QuotingPricing

  @type line_item :: QuotingPricing.line_item()

  @type summary :: %{
          line_items: [line_item()],
          add_on_items: [line_item()],
          subtotal_cents: integer(),
          discount_percent: integer(),
          total_cents: integer(),
          priceable?: boolean()
        }

  @doc """
  Every number `CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.Quote` needs to render the
  live total in one call.
  """
  @spec summarize(RateCard.t(), Lead.t()) :: summary()
  def summarize(%RateCard{} = rate_card, %Lead{} = lead) do
    line_items = base_line_items(rate_card, lead)
    add_on_items = add_on_line_items(rate_card, lead)
    subtotal_cents = QuotingPricing.total_cents(line_items) + QuotingPricing.total_cents(add_on_items)
    discount_percent = discount_percent(rate_card, lead)

    %{
      line_items: line_items,
      add_on_items: add_on_items,
      subtotal_cents: subtotal_cents,
      discount_percent: discount_percent,
      total_cents: apply_discount(subtotal_cents, discount_percent),
      priceable?: priceable?(line_items, add_on_items)
    }
  end

  @doc "The base (room/sqft/hourly) line items, priced the same way an office quote is."
  @spec base_line_items(RateCard.t(), Lead.t()) :: [line_item()]
  def base_line_items(%RateCard{} = rate_card, %Lead{} = lead) do
    QuotingPricing.line_items(rate_card, %Quote{
      pricing_model: lead.pricing_model,
      bedroom_count: lead.bedroom_count,
      bathroom_count: lead.bathroom_count,
      square_feet: lead.square_feet,
      hours: lead.hours
    })
  end

  @doc """
  One line item per selected add-on, `rate_cents: nil` when the rate
  card hasn't configured a price for it yet — the same "never guess"
  rule `CleanerCrm.Quoting.Pricing.missing_rate?/1` applies to the base
  rates.
  """
  @spec add_on_line_items(RateCard.t(), Lead.t()) :: [line_item()]
  def add_on_line_items(%RateCard{add_on_rates_cents: rates}, %Lead{add_ons: add_ons}) do
    Enum.map(add_ons, fn key ->
      rate_cents = Map.get(rates || %{}, key)

      %{
        description: humanize(key),
        quantity: 1,
        rate_cents: rate_cents,
        amount_cents: rate_cents || 0
      }
    end)
  end

  @doc """
  Whether this lead is priceable at all: at least one priced base line
  item, and no selected item (base or add-on) missing a rate.
  """
  @spec priceable?(RateCard.t(), Lead.t()) :: boolean()
  def priceable?(%RateCard{} = rate_card, %Lead{} = lead) do
    priceable?(base_line_items(rate_card, lead), add_on_line_items(rate_card, lead))
  end

  defp priceable?(line_items, add_on_items) do
    line_items != [] and
      not QuotingPricing.missing_rate?(line_items) and
      not QuotingPricing.missing_rate?(add_on_items)
  end

  @doc "The discount percent (0 when unset) the rate card configures for a lead's frequency."
  @spec discount_percent(RateCard.t(), Lead.t()) :: integer()
  def discount_percent(%RateCard{} = rate_card, %Lead{frequency: frequency}) do
    case frequency do
      :weekly -> rate_card.weekly_discount_percent || 0
      :biweekly -> rate_card.biweekly_discount_percent || 0
      :monthly -> rate_card.monthly_discount_percent || 0
      _one_time_or_nil -> 0
    end
  end

  defp apply_discount(subtotal_cents, 0), do: subtotal_cents

  defp apply_discount(subtotal_cents, discount_percent) do
    subtotal_cents
    |> Decimal.new()
    |> Decimal.mult(Decimal.new(100 - discount_percent))
    |> Decimal.div(Decimal.new(100))
    |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up)
    |> Decimal.to_integer()
  end

  defp humanize(key) do
    key
    |> String.replace("_", " ")
    |> String.capitalize()
  end
end
